children.title: Original Variable Space
children.top_down_role: Coordinates, geometry, and interpretation in the represented space.

knowledge_statements.title: Original Variable Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the unlifted ambient space whose feasible points are recovered by projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(Y=\mathbb{R}^q\) be an auxiliary space. For a lifted feasible set \(L\subseteq X\times Y\), the original variable space is the first factor \(X\). The set represented in original variables is
\[
C=\operatorname{proj}_X(L)=\{x\in X:\exists y\in Y,\ (x,y)\in L\}.
\]
Thus only \(x\) belongs to the represented set; auxiliary coordinates are existential witnesses and are discarded after projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The original variable space contains the modeled decisions. A point is represented exactly when it has at least one feasible auxiliary witness in the lifted set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=\{x\in X:\exists y\in Y,\ (x,y)\in L\}\).

source_refs.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

source_witnesses.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

children.title: Auxiliary Variable Space
children.top_down_role: Lift coordinates, dimensional choices, and witness structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary Variable Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the existential witness coordinates introduced by a lifted representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(Y=\mathbb{R}^q\). In a lifted representation \(L\subseteq X\times Y\), the auxiliary variable space is the second factor \(Y\). For each \(x\in X\), its admissible auxiliary witnesses form the fiber
\[
L_x=\{y\in Y:(x,y)\in L\}.
\]
Auxiliary variables do not enlarge the represented variable tuple: they certify membership through the equivalence \(x\in\operatorname{proj}_X(L)\) if and only if \(L_x\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The auxiliary space contains witness variables. An original point is represented precisely when its set of feasible auxiliary witnesses is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\operatorname{proj}_X(L)\iff L_x\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Fiber of feasible witnesses over an original point.

source_refs.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

source_witnesses.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

children.title: Original-to-Auxiliary Space Interface
children.top_down_role: Structural links between represented coordinates and lift coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Original-to-Auxiliary Space Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the existential interface joining original and auxiliary coordinates through conic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), \(Y=\mathbb{R}^q\), let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be a convex cone, let \(A:X\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(B:Y\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be linear, and let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). The affine-conic interface is
\[
L=\{(x,y)\in X\times Y:Ax+By+b\in K\}.
\]
It represents \(C\subseteq X\) exactly when
\[
x\in C\iff \exists y\in Y\text{ such that }Ax+By+b\in K.
\]
For \(x\in X\), define \(L_x=\{y\in Y:(x,y)\in L\}\). The set-valued map \(x\mapsto L_x\) assigns all valid conic witnesses to each original point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine conic constraint couples original and auxiliary variables. Projection is exact when original membership is equivalent to the existence of a feasible auxiliary witness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=\{x\in X:\exists y\in Y,\ Ax+By+b\in K\}\).

notation.meaning: Linear maps coupling original and auxiliary variables.
Affine offset in the conic constraint.
Set of valid auxiliary witnesses for x.

source_refs.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

children.title: Coordinate Projection View
children.top_down_role: Coordinate elimination as the visible-space interpretation of a lift.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Projection View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses a lifted set as the coordinate projection of a higher-dimensional feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L\subseteq X\times Y\), where \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces, and let \(\pi_X:X\times Y\to X\) satisfy \(\pi_X(x,y)=x\). The coordinate-projection representation of \(C\subseteq X\) is
\[
C=\pi_X(L)=\{x\in X:\exists y\in Y,\ (x,y)\in L\}.
\]
If \(L\) is convex, then \(C\) is convex. If \(L\) is given by affine membership in a convex cone, this equality is a lifted-conic representation of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A represented set is obtained by retaining original coordinates and discarding auxiliary coordinates. Convexity is preserved under this projection.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=\pi_X(L)\), and \(L\) convex implies \(C\) convex.

children.title: General Linear-Image View
children.top_down_role: Represented sets obtained through arbitrary linear image maps.

knowledge_statements.title: General Linear-Image View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies arbitrary linear images with coordinate projections of graph lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z\) and \(X\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(D\subseteq Z\), and let \(P:Z\to X\) be linear. Define the graph lift
\[
L_P=\{(Pz,z)\in X\times Z:z\in D\}.
\]
Then
\[
P(D)=\operatorname{proj}_X(L_P).
\]
Conversely, every coordinate projection \(\operatorname{proj}_X(L)\) is the linear image of \(L\) under \(\operatorname{proj}_X\). Hence linear-image and coordinate-projection descriptions are equivalent after introducing graph coordinates; convexity is preserved when \(D\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every linear image can be written as a coordinate projection of a graph lift, and every coordinate projection is itself a linear image.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(D)=\operatorname{proj}_X\{(Pz,z):z\in D\}\).

notation.meaning: Graph lift associated with the image map.

children.title: Fiber Structure
children.top_down_role: Lifted witnesses sharing a common visible image.

knowledge_statements.title: Fiber Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes projection membership and convexity through fibers over original points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(L\subseteq X\times Y\) and \(x\in X\), define the fiber
\[
L_x=\{y\in Y:(x,y)\in L\}.
\]
Then the projected set is exactly
\[
\operatorname{proj}_X(L)=\{x\in X:L_x\neq\varnothing\}.
\]
If \(L\) is convex, every fiber \(L_x\) is convex because it is identified with the intersection of \(L\) and the affine slice \(\{x\}\times Y\). Distinct auxiliary witnesses in the same fiber represent the same original point, so uniqueness of a lift is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection membership means that the corresponding fiber is nonempty. Fibers of a convex lifted set are convex, and witnesses need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\operatorname{proj}_X(L)\iff L_x\neq\varnothing\); if \(L\) is convex, then \(L_x\) is convex.

notation.meaning: Auxiliary fiber over the original point.

source_refs.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

children.title: Image Recovery Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cases where image descriptions obscure or fail to preserve desired witness information.

knowledge_statements.title: Image Recovery Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marks the failure of exact recovery from closure when a linear image is nonclosed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Exact image recovery requires an actual preimage, not merely membership in the closure of the image. Let
\[
L=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2:x>0,\ y\geq 1/x\}.
\]
For \(a\in\mathbb{R}\), define the fiber \(L_a=\{y\in\mathbb{R}:(a,y)\in L\}\). The set \(L\) is closed and convex, but
\[
\operatorname{proj}_x(L)=(0,\infty),
\]
which is not closed. Hence \(0\in\overline{\operatorname{proj}_x(L)}\) while \(L_0=\varnothing\). Replacing a projected image by its closure can therefore introduce points having no finite lifted witness; closedness of the lifted set alone does not prevent this failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex lift may have a nonclosed image. Boundary points added by closure can lack any finite auxiliary witness and therefore are not exactly represented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\overline{\operatorname{proj}_x(L)}\setminus\operatorname{proj}_x(L)\) and \(L_0=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Fiber of the lift over first coordinate a.

children.title: Affine Preimage View
children.top_down_role: Representations pulled back through affine maps.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Preimage View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents a set as the inverse image of a cone under an affine map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Z\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(K\subseteq Z\) be a convex cone, and let \(F:X\to Z\) be affine with \(F(x)=Ax+b\), where \(A:X\to Z\) is linear and \(b\in Z\). The affine-preimage representation is
\[
C=F^{-1}(K)=\{x\in X:Ax+b\in K\}.
\]
The set \(C\) is convex. More generally, let \(Y\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(B:Y\to Z\) be linear. Then auxiliary variables give
\[
C=\{x\in X:\exists y\in Y,\ Ax+By+b\in K\},
\]
which is the projection of an affine preimage in \(X\times Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine-preimage model pulls a cone back to the original space. Adding a declared auxiliary space and linear auxiliary map converts the preimage into a projected conic lift.
assumptions_latex: \(X\), \(Y\), and \(Z\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=F^{-1}(K)=\{x\in X:Ax+b\in K\}\) is convex.

notation.meaning: Affine map into the conic ambient space.
Linear maps from the original and auxiliary spaces into Z.

source_refs.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

source_witnesses.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

children.title: Linear Embedding View
children.top_down_role: Represented objects placed inside a higher-dimensional ambient space.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Embedding View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts an affine preimage into a linear embedding on homogenized coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Z\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(A:X\to Z\) be linear, and let \(b\in Z\). Define the affine map \(F:X\to Z\) by \(F(x)=Ax+b\). Introduce the homogenized slice \(H=\{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb{R}:t=1\}\) and the linear map \(E:X\times\mathbb{R}\to X\times Z\times\mathbb{R}\) given by
\[
E(x,t)=(x,Ax+tb,t).
\]
The restriction of \(E\) to \(H\) is injective, and for every \(K\subseteq Z\),
\[
\{x\in X:Ax+b\in K\}
=
\{x\in X:E(x,1)\in X\times K\times\{1\}\}.
\]
Thus affine-preimage constraints can be viewed as intersections of a linearly embedded image with a target set on the homogenizing slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenization turns an affine map into a linear embedding with an explicit product-space codomain. The original feasible set is recovered by imposing the target constraint on the embedded slice.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Z\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^{-1}(K)=\{x\in X:E(x,1)\in X\times K\times\{1\}\}\).

notation.meaning: Linear embedding from homogenized coordinates into the product space.

source_refs.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

source_witnesses.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

children.title: Embedding Image Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between embedded copies and their visible-space images.

knowledge_statements.title: Embedding Image Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the exact intersection condition required for recovery through an injective embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E:X\to Z\) be injective, let \(S\subseteq X\), and let \(Q\subseteq Z\). The target set \(Q\) is compatible with the embedded representation of \(S\) precisely when
\[
Q\cap E(X)=E(S).
\]
Under this condition,
\[
S=E^{-1}(Q).
\]
Conversely, \(S=E^{-1}(Q)\) implies \(Q\cap E(X)=E(S)\). Points of \(Q\setminus E(X)\) are irrelevant to recovery, while an omitted or additional point in \(Q\cap E(X)\) causes corresponding failure of exact recovery in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An embedded representation is exact precisely when the target set intersects the embedding image in exactly the image of the represented set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=E^{-1}(Q)\iff Q\cap E(X)=E(S)\).

notation.meaning: Target set in the embedding space.

source_refs.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

source_witnesses.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

children.title: Epigraph Lifts
children.top_down_role: Lifted upper-value descriptions for convex functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines an exact conic lift of the epigraph of a convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex. An epigraph lift of \(f\) consists of an auxiliary space \(Y\), a convex cone \(K\subseteq Z\), linear maps \(A:X\to Z\), \(B:Y\to Z\), a vector \(c\in Z\), and \(d\in Z\) such that
\[
\operatorname{epi}f
=
\{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb{R}:\exists y\in Y,\ Ax+By+tc+d\in K\}.
\]
Consequently, \(f(x)\leq t\) holds exactly when the displayed conic system admits an auxiliary witness \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epigraph lift represents the inequality defining a convex function's epigraph as the projection of an affine-conic feasible set with auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)\leq t\iff \exists y\in Y,\ Ax+By+tc+d\in K\).

source_refs.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

source_witnesses.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

children.title: Hypograph Lifts
children.top_down_role: Lifted lower-value descriptions for concave functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Hypograph Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines an exact conic lift of the hypograph of a concave function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}\) be proper and concave. A hypograph lift of \(g\) consists of an auxiliary space \(Y\), a convex cone \(K\subseteq Z\), linear maps \(A:X\to Z\), \(B:Y\to Z\), a vector \(c\in Z\), and \(d\in Z\) such that
\[
\operatorname{hypo}g
=
\{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb{R}:\exists y\in Y,\ Ax+By+tc+d\in K\}.
\]
Consequently, \(t\leq g(x)\) holds exactly when the displayed conic system admits an auxiliary witness \(y\). Equivalently, a hypograph lift of \(g\) is an epigraph lift of \(-g\) after replacing \(t\) by \(-t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hypograph lift represents a concave function's lower-value inequality as the projection of an affine-conic feasible set with auxiliary witnesses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\leq g(x)\iff \exists y\in Y,\ Ax+By+tc+d\in K\).

source_refs.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

source_witnesses.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

children.title: Graph Recovery Interface
children.top_down_role: Boundary-value recovery from lifted epi- or hypographic descriptions.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is convex and concave on a convex domain \(D\subseteq X\).
\(E,H\) are lifted sets whose projections are respectively \(\operatorname{epi}f\) and \(\operatorname{hypo}f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{gph}f=\{(x,r):\exists u,v,\ (x,r,u)\in E,\ (x,r,v)\in H\}\).

notation.meaning: epigraph and hypograph lifted feasible sets

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a graph is recovered by imposing compatible epigraph and hypograph representations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact graph recovery from compatible epigraph and hypograph lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\pi_{x,r}(E)=\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,r)\in D\times\mathbb R:f(x)\le r\}\) and \(\pi_{x,r}(H)=\operatorname{hypo}f=\{(x,r)\in D\times\mathbb R:r\le f(x)\}\). Then the common-value interface is
\[
\operatorname{gph}f=\operatorname{epi}f\cap\operatorname{hypo}f
=\{(x,r)\in D\times\mathbb R:\exists u,v,\ (x,r,u)\in E,\ (x,r,v)\in H\}.
\]
Thus the two lifted systems recover the graph exactly when they share the same original variables \((x,r)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting compatible lifted epigraph and hypograph formulations forces the ordinate to equal the function value, thereby recovering the graph exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph Recovery Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The graph-intersection representation fits the leaf and is mathematically standard, but no inspectable citation is supplied. The ambient spaces for the auxiliary variables u and v should also be stated when sourcing the record.

children.title: Slack-Variable Lifts
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary slack coordinates used to expose conic membership or equality structure.

assumptions_latex: \(A:X\to Y\) is linear, \(b\in Y\), and \(K\subseteq Y\) is a convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b-Ax\in K\iff \exists s\in K\text{ such that }Ax+s=b\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conic inclusion and conic slack equality are algebraically equivalent
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-form lift of a finite-dimensional conic inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the conic inequality \(b-Ax\in K\), introduce an auxiliary variable \(s\in Y\). Its slack-variable lift is
\[
\mathcal L=\{(x,s)\in X\times Y:Ax+s=b,\ s\in K\}.
\]
The original feasible set is recovered by projection:
\[
\{x\in X:b-Ax\in K\}=\pi_x(\mathcal L).
\]
For componentwise inequalities, taking \(K=\mathbb R_+^m\) gives the familiar nonnegative slack \(s=b-Ax\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic inequality is equivalently written as a linear equality after introducing a slack constrained to the ordering cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Variable Lifts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conic slack representation is precise, internally consistent, and appropriate for the container, but it has no inspectable source or locator.

children.title: Split-Variable Lifts
children.top_down_role: Variable decompositions used to separate signs, blocks, or structural components.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=x^+-x^-\) with \(x^+,x^-\in\mathbb R_+^n\), and every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) admits such a lift.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: splitting a free vector into two nonnegative vectors is a standard conic lift
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative split lift for unrestricted finite-dimensional variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The split-variable lift of a free vector \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) introduces \(x^+,x^-\in\mathbb R_+^n\) and imposes
\[
x=x^+-x^-.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\mathbb R^n=\{x^+-x^-:(x^+,x^-)\in\mathbb R_+^n\times\mathbb R_+^n\}.
\]
One canonical choice is \(x_i^+=\max\{x_i,0\}\) and \(x_i^-=\max\{-x_i,0\}\), although the lifted representation need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every unrestricted vector is the difference of two nonnegative vectors, permitting models over a nonnegative cone at the cost of auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Split-Variable Lifts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonnegative split-variable representation is correct and appropriately classified, but no cited source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Slack Elimination Interface
children.top_down_role: Visible-space recovery after removal of slack coordinates.

assumptions_latex: \(A:X\to Y\) is linear, \(b\in Y\), and \(K\subseteq Y\) is a convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eliminating \(s\) from \(Ax+s=b,\ s\in K\) yields exactly \(b-Ax\in K\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: substitution uniquely eliminates an equality-defined slack variable
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection and substitution interface for conic slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(\mathcal L=\{(x,s):Ax+s=b,\ s\in K\}\). The equality determines the auxiliary variable uniquely as \(s=b-Ax\). Consequently,
\[
\pi_x(\mathcal L)=\{x:\exists s\in K,\ Ax+s=b\}=\{x:b-Ax\in K\}.
\]
Thus substitution eliminates the slack without changing feasibility in the original variable. Any objective depending only on \(x\) has the same feasible objective values before and after this elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slack defined by a linear equality can be substituted out; projection of the lifted system exactly restores the original conic inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: Slack Elimination Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The elimination and projection property is correctly stated and matches the interface leaf, but it lacks an inspectable citation.

children.title: Split Consistency Boundary
children.top_down_role: Consistency requirements limiting valid split-variable representations.

assumptions_latex: The intended split represents \(x\in\mathbb R\) by nonnegative variables \(x^+,x^-\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without \(x=x^+-x^-\), projection onto \(x\) can strictly enlarge the represented feasible set.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the linking equality is necessary for the split variables to represent the original variable
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by omitting the split-variable linking equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Nonnegativity of \(x^+\) and \(x^-\) alone does not make them a lift of \(x\); the consistency equation \(x=x^+-x^-\) is essential. For example, the original constraint \(x=1\) may be written as \(x^+-x^-=1\) together with \(x=x^+-x^-\) and \(x^+,x^-\ge0\). If the linking equation involving \(x\) is omitted, the lifted constraints remain feasible independently of \(x\), and their projection onto \(x\) becomes all of \(\mathbb R\), not \(\{1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dropping the equation linking a variable to its positive-minus-negative split decouples the lift and can enlarge the projected feasible set arbitrarily.
knowledge_statements.title: Split Consistency Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly identifies failure after removal of the linking equation and fits a failure-boundary container, but no source with a locator is supplied.

children.title: Perspective Lifts
children.top_down_role: Scaled function or set representations using perspective coordinates.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted inequality \(t f(x/t)\le\eta\) is convex in \((x,t,\eta)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the perspective of a proper convex function is convex on positive scales
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-scale perspective epigraph lift of a convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The positive-scale perspective of \(f\) is
\[
f^{\pi}(x,t)=t f(x/t),\qquad t>0.
\]
Its epigraph lift is
\[
\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}=\{(x,t,\eta):t>0,\ t f(x/t)\le\eta\}.
\]
This set is convex. At the normalization slice \(t=1\), it recovers the original epigraph:
\[
\{(x,\eta):(x,1,\eta)\in\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}\}=\operatorname{epi}f.
\]
A closed extension to \(t=0\) requires the recession value rather than direct division by \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling both the argument and function value produces a convex perspective epigraph whose unit-scale slice is the original epigraph.
knowledge_statements.title: Perspective Lifts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-scale perspective formulation and unit-scale recovery statement are standard and correctly separated from the zero-scale extension, but they lack an inspectable citation.

children.title: Homogenizing Lifts
children.top_down_role: Conic representations formed by introducing a homogenizing coordinate.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_C=\operatorname{cl}\{(tx,t):x\in C,\ t>0\}\) is a closed convex cone encoding \(C\).

notation.meaning: closed homogenization cone of the set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conic homogenization embeds a convex set as a unit slice of a cone
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed conic homogenization of a convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The closed homogenizing lift of \(C\) is
\[
K_C=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}\{(x,1):x\in C\}
=\operatorname{cl}\{(tx,t):x\in C,\ t>0\}.
\]
The set \(K_C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}\) is a closed convex cone. For every \(t>0\), membership satisfies
\[
(y,t)\in K_C\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y/t\in\operatorname{cl}C,
\]
with \(C\) replacing \(\operatorname{cl}C\) when \(C\) is closed. The additional face at \(t=0\) records recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenization embeds a convex set into one higher dimension as a cone; positive-scale points correspond to scaled points of the original set.
knowledge_statements.title: Homogenizing Lifts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closed homogenization cone and its positive-scale interpretation are correctly stated for a nonempty convex set, but no supporting source and locator are provided.

children.title: Dehomogenization Slice
children.top_down_role: Affine slices used to recover the original nonhomogeneous object.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:(x,1)\in K_C\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: intersecting the homogenization cone with the unit-scale hyperplane recovers the closed convex set
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unit-scale recovery slice for a homogenized closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The affine hyperplane \(\{(x,t):t=1\}\) is the dehomogenization slice of \(K_C\). It recovers the original set exactly:
\[
C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:(x,1)\in K_C\}.
\]
More generally, any point \((y,t)\in K_C\) with \(t>0\) dehomogenizes to \(y/t\in C\). Hence positive rescaling along a ray of \(K_C\) does not change its dehomogenized representative, while points on the face \(t=0\) cannot be dehomogenized by division.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting a homogenization cone with the unit-scale hyperplane recovers the original closed convex set; other positive-scale points normalize by division.
knowledge_statements.title: Dehomogenization Slice

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unit-scale slice exactly recovers a closed convex set and fits the representation container, but the record has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Zero-Scale Boundary
children.top_down_role: Degenerate scaling regimes affecting perspective or homogenized recovery.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_C\cap(\mathbb R^n\times\{0\})=\operatorname{rec}(C)\times\{0\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the zero-scale face of a closed homogenization cone equals the recession cone
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretation of the zero-scale face of a homogenization cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At zero scale, homogenization records asymptotic directions rather than ordinary points:
\[
K_C\cap(\mathbb R^n\times\{0\})=\operatorname{rec}(C)\times\{0\},
\]
where
\[
\operatorname{rec}(C)=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:x+\lambda d\in C\text{ for every }x\in C\text{ and }\lambda\ge0\}.
\]
Thus \((d,0)\in K_C\) cannot be normalized by division. The zero-scale face is trivial exactly when \(C\) contains no nonzero recession direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zero-scale face of a closed homogenization cone consists precisely of recession directions, so its points generally cannot be dehomogenized.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Scale Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The zero-scale face characterization is mathematically appropriate for a nonempty closed convex set and fits the boundary leaf, but it lacks a cited source with a locator.

children.title: Matrix-Variable Lifts
children.top_down_role: Higher-dimensional matrix variables used to expose convex structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Variable Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite matrix lift and relaxation of quadratic products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quadratic matrix expression \(xx^\top\) can be lifted to a symmetric variable \(X\in\mathbb S^n\). The block constraint
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0
\]
is equivalent to \(X-xx^\top\succeq0\). Exact consistency with the quadratic product is imposed by the nonconvex equality \(X=xx^\top\). Replacing that equality by \(X-xx^\top\succeq0\) gives the associated semidefinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric matrix variable can replace the quadratic product of a vector with itself. Equality with that product gives an exact lift, while the block positive-semidefinite constraint gives a convex relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\iff X-xx^\top\succeq0\), while exact quadratic consistency is \(X=xx^\top\).

children.title: Gram Lifts
children.top_down_role: Inner-product encodings through positive-semidefinite Gram matrices.

assumptions_latex: \(z(x)\) is a fixed finite vector of real monomials.
\(p\) is a real polynomial whose degree does not exceed twice the largest degree in \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\) is a sum of squares in the span of \(z\) iff \(p(x)=z(x)^\top Qz(x)\) for some \(Q\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite Gram representation of a sum-of-squares polynomial.

source_refs.locator: 8.4 A Gram-like Representation p. 370
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The polynomial \(p\) is a sum of squares of polynomials from \(\operatorname{span}z\) if and only if there exists a symmetric matrix \(Q\succeq0\) such that
\[
p(x)=z(x)^\top Qz(x).
\]
Equality means coefficientwise equality of polynomials and therefore imposes affine equations on \(Q\). A factorization \(Q=R^\top R\) yields \(p(x)=\sum_i(Rz(x))_i^2\). Different positive-semidefinite matrices may represent the same polynomial because coefficient matching need not determine \(Q\) uniquely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial is sum-of-squares in a chosen monomial span exactly when it has a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix satisfying coefficient-matching equations.
knowledge_statements.title: Gram Lifts

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gram matrices: positivity, rank, and the stated converse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a Gram matrix and preserves the extract’s positive-definite hypothesis in the converse direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For vectors $v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb{R}^d$, define $X=(x_{ij})$ by $x_{ij}=\langle v_i,v_j\rangle$. Then $X\succeq0$ and $\operatorname{rank}X=\dim\operatorname{span}\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\}\le d$. Conversely, as stated in the extract, if $X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is positive definite and $\operatorname{rank}X\le d$, then there exist $v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb{R}^d$ such that $x_{ij}=\langle v_i,v_j\rangle$ for all $i,j$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gram matrix records all pairwise inner products of a finite vector family. It is positive semidefinite, and its rank is the dimension of the vectors’ span. The extract also gives a converse under the stronger assumption that the matrix is positive definite and has rank at most d.
assumptions_latex: X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\text{ is positive definite and }\operatorname{rank}X\le d\text{ in the converse direction}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\succeq0,\quad \operatorname{rank}X=\dim\operatorname{span}\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\}\le d;\qquad \exists v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb{R}^d:\ X=(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle)_{i,j}\text{ under the converse assumptions}.

children.title: Moment Lifts
children.top_down_role: Moment-coordinate representations for polynomial or measure-based structure.

assumptions_latex: \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le2d}\) is a truncated real multisequence with \(y_0=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_d(y)_{\alpha,\beta}=y_{\alpha+\beta}\), and any representing probability measure implies \(M_d(y)\succeq0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: moment matrices linearly lift monomial products and are positive semidefinite for representing measures
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated moment-matrix lift for polynomial data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the moment matrix indexed by monomials of degree at most \(d\) by
\[
M_d(y)_{\alpha,\beta}=y_{\alpha+\beta}.
\]
If a probability measure \(\mu\) represents the sequence, meaning \(y_\gamma=\int x^\gamma\,d\mu(x)\) for every \(|\gamma|\le2d\), then
\[
M_d(y)=\int v_d(x)v_d(x)^\top\,d\mu(x)\succeq0.
\]
For a point mass at \(x\), the lift is rank one: \(M_d(y)=v_d(x)v_d(x)^\top\). Positive semidefiniteness alone is generally necessary but not sufficient for a representing measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated moment sequence lifts to a matrix whose entries are moments; representing measures produce positive-semidefinite matrices, with point masses producing rank-one matrices.
knowledge_statements.title: Moment Lifts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The moment-matrix construction, positive-semidefinite necessity, rank-one point-mass case, and insufficiency caveat are correctly stated, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Low-Rank Recovery Boundary
children.top_down_role: Rank restrictions separating exact lifted objects from convex relaxations.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform exact recovery holds precisely under the strict rank-(r) null-space inequality; equality or reversal is the boundary at which uniqueness can fail.

notation.meaning: Singular values of (H) in nonincreasing order.

review_flags: Exact matrix null-space-property source is absent from the supplied locator hints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform noiseless recovery of all matrices having rank at most (r) by nuclear-norm minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let (q=\min\{m,n\}). Every matrix (X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}) with (\operatorname{rank}X\le r) is the unique solution of [\min_Z\ \|Z\|_*\quad\text{subject to}\quad A(Z)=A(X)] if and only if every nonzero (H\in\ker A) satisfies [\sum_{i=1}^{r}\sigma_i(H)<\sum_{i=r+1}^{q}\sigma_i(H).] If this strict inequality fails for some null-space direction, there exists a matrix of rank at most (r) for which nuclear-norm minimization does not give unique exact recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform rank-r nuclear-norm recovery holds exactly when every nonzero measurement-null direction has less singular-value mass in its largest r values than in the remainder.
knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Recovery Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The null-space characterization is mathematically plausible and fits the failure-boundary leaf, but this nontrivial iff theorem has no citation. A source specifically supporting the matrix rank-r nuclear-norm null-space property is required; delimiter defects can be repaired after sourcing.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Extensions of Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-projection definition of a finite-dimensional exact convex extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The lifted set \(Q\) is an exact extension of \(C\) under \(\pi_x\) when \[C=\pi_x(Q)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists y\in\mathbb{R}^k\text{ such that }(x,y)\in Q\}.\] Equivalently, every lifted feasible point projects into \(C\), and every point of \(C\) has at least one lifted feasible witness. If \(Q\) is described by affine equations and membership in a closed convex cone, this equality is an exact lifted-conic formulation of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted convex set exactly extends a set when its projection is precisely the original set, with neither missing points nor extraneous projected points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\) is an exact extension of \(C\) exactly when \(C=\pi_x(Q)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Extensions of Function Epigraphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lifting of a proper convex function through its epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set \(Q\) is an exact extension of the epigraph of \(f\) when \[\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1}:t\ge f(x)\}=\{(x,t):\exists y\in\mathbb{R}^k,\ (x,t,y)\in Q\}.\] Thus \[f(x)=\inf\{t:\exists y\in\mathbb{R}^k,\ (x,t,y)\in Q\},\] with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). Exact epigraph projection represents both the function values and the effective domain of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted set exactly represents a convex function when projecting away its auxiliary variables yields exactly the function's epigraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\) exactly extends the epigraph precisely when \(\pi_{x,t}(Q)=\operatorname{epi}f\).

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization-Equivalent Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Problem-level equivalence, which need not imply equality of the entire projected feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(v=\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\) and \(\widehat v=\inf_{(x,y)\in Q}F(x,y)\). The lifted problem is optimization-equivalent to the original problem when \(v=\widehat v\) and \[\pi_x\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in Q}F(x,y)\right)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x).\] This permits \(\pi_x(Q)\ne C\), provided the additional or omitted projected points alter neither the optimal value nor the projected optimizer set for the specified objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two formulations are optimization-equivalent when they have the same infimum and their lifted optimizers project exactly onto the original optimizers, including the case in which both optimizer sets are empty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted problem is optimization-equivalent when its optimal value and projected optimizer set agree with those of the original problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer Lifted Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer approximation produced by projecting a tractable lifted convex feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The lifted set \(Q_{\mathrm{out}}\) defines an outer lifted relaxation of \(C\) if \[C\subseteq C_{\mathrm{out}}:=\pi_x(Q_{\mathrm{out}})=\{x:\exists y,\ (x,y)\in Q_{\mathrm{out}}\}.\] Consequently, for every extended-real objective \(f\) defined on \(C_{\mathrm{out}}\), \[\inf_{x\in C_{\mathrm{out}}}f(x)\le\inf_{x\in C}f(x).\] Equality is not required. Approximation accuracy requires an additional metric-containment or objective-gap bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer lifted relaxation projects to a superset of the target set, so minimization over it supplies a lower bound but may introduce spurious solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_{\mathrm{out}}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+k}\) is a tractable convex lifted set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining guarantee is \(C\subseteq\pi_x(Q_{\mathrm{out}})\); minimization over the projection gives a lower bound for every common objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner Lifted Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner approximation obtained as the projection of a tractable lifted convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The lifted set \(Q_{\mathrm{in}}\) defines an inner lifted approximation of \(C\) if \[C_{\mathrm{in}}:=\pi_x(Q_{\mathrm{in}})=\{x:\exists y,\ (x,y)\in Q_{\mathrm{in}}\}\subseteq C.\] Hence every projected lifted point is feasible for the original problem. If \(C_{\mathrm{in}}\ne\varnothing\), then for every extended-real objective \(f\) on \(C\), \[\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\le\inf_{x\in C_{\mathrm{in}}}f(x).\] The inclusion alone does not guarantee proximity to the original optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner lifted approximation projects inside the target set, producing certified feasible points and an upper bound for minimization, but possibly excluding good solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_{\mathrm{in}}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+k}\) is a tractable convex lifted set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining guarantee is \(\pi_x(Q_{\mathrm{in}})\subseteq C\); minimization over the projection gives an upper bound whenever it is nonempty.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Specific Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-preserving lift tailored to one specified minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair \((Q_f,F_f)\) is an objective-specific extension of \(\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\) when \[\inf_{(x,y)\in Q_f}F_f(x,y)=\inf_{x\in C}f(x).\] If optimizer recovery is claimed, one additionally requires \[\pi_x\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in Q_f}F_f(x,y)\right)\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x).\] Neither \(\pi_x(Q_f)=C\) nor preservation of optimal values for objectives other than \(f\) follows from objective-specific equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective-specific extension preserves one chosen optimization problem's value, and optionally supports optimizer recovery, without necessarily representing the original feasible set exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The extension is objective-specific when it preserves the infimum for this \(f\), without requiring exact projected-set equality or equivalence for other objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Feasible-Set Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-inclusion certificate for exact equivalence between an original set and a projected lifted set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A projected feasible-set equivalence certificate consists of verifiable witnesses for both inclusions: \[\forall (x,y)\in Q,\quad x\in C,\] and \[\forall x\in C,\quad \exists y_x\in\mathbb{R}^k\text{ with }(x,y_x)\in Q.\] The first obligation excludes spurious projected points; the second proves liftability of every original feasible point. Together they imply \(\pi_x(Q)\subseteq C\) and \(C\subseteq\pi_x(Q)\), hence \(C=\pi_x(Q)\). A constructive rule \(x\mapsto y_x\) is sufficient but not necessary for the second obligation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact projected feasibility is certified by showing every lifted point projects feasibly and every original feasible point admits a lifted witness.
assumptions_latex: Membership and feasibility predicates for both sets are independently checkable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two witness obligations certify \(C=\pi_x(Q)\).

children.title: Objective Representation
children.top_down_role: Placement and evaluation of the original objective within the lifted formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real objective represented by partial minimization over each lifted fiber.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define the fiber \[Q_x=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^k:(x,y)\in Q\}.\] The lifted pair \((Q,F)\) represents the extended-real objective \(f\) when \[f(x)=\inf_{y\in Q_x}F(x,y)\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\] where \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). Thus the represented objective is obtained by partial minimization over the auxiliary variables; no attainment of the fiber infimum is implied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted objective represents the original objective when minimizing it over each auxiliary-variable fiber gives the original extended-real value; the fiber infimum need not be attained.
assumptions_latex: \(F:Q\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is the lifted objective, and its fiber infima are not \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The represented objective is the fiberwise infimum \(f(x)=\inf_{y:(x,y)\in Q}F(x,y)\).

children.title: Optimal-Value Preservation
children.top_down_role: Exact agreement of original and lifted optimal values.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Value Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infimal-value preservation under exact projected feasibility and exact fiberwise objective representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+k}\), \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), and \(F:Q\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\). If \(C=\pi_x(Q)\) and \[f(x)=\inf\{F(x,y):(x,y)\in Q\}\quad\text{for every }x\in C,\] then \[\inf_{x\in C}f(x)=\inf_{x\in C}\inf_{y:(x,y)\in Q}F(x,y)=\inf_{(x,y)\in Q}F(x,y).\] This preserves the extended-real optimal value but does not assert attainment or the existence of an optimal auxiliary witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact projected feasibility and fiberwise objective representation imply equality of the original and lifted infima, but do not by themselves guarantee attainment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in C}f(x)=\inf_{(x,y)\in Q}F(x,y)\), including extended-real values.

children.title: Attainment Preservation
children.top_down_role: Transfer of optimizer existence between original and lifted formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Attainment Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-way optimizer correspondence when every fiber minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+k}\), \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), and \(F:Q\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\). Suppose \(C=\pi_x(Q)\) and, for every \(x\in C\), the fiber minimum exists and satisfies \[f(x)=\min\{F(x,y):(x,y)\in Q\}.\] If \[S=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\ne\varnothing,\] then \[\widehat S=\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in Q}F(x,y)\ne\varnothing\quad\text{and}\quad\pi_x(\widehat S)=S.\] Without fiber attainment, value preservation need not produce a lifted optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every auxiliary fiber attains its represented value and the original problem has a minimizer, original minimizers lift to lifted minimizers and all lifted minimizers project back exactly.
assumptions_latex: For every \(x\in C\), the minimum \(f(x)=\min_{y:(x,y)\in Q}F(x,y)\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both minima are attained and \(\pi_x(\operatorname*{argmin}_{Q}F)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{C}f\).

children.title: Objective Distortion Boundary
children.top_down_role: Formulation changes that alter objective values or attainment behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Distortion Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp conversion of uniform objective-representation error into optimal-value error on a common feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(v_f=\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\) and \(v_g=\inf_{x\in C}g(x)\), and assume \(v_f\in\mathbb{R}\). Uniform distortion \[\sup_{x\in C}|g(x)-f(x)|\le\varepsilon\] implies \(v_g\in\mathbb{R}\) and \[|v_g-v_f|\le\varepsilon.\] The constant is sharp: for any nonempty \(C\), taking \(g=f+\varepsilon\) gives \(v_g-v_f=\varepsilon\). Without a uniform or optimizer-relevant error bound, the optimal-value gap can be arbitrarily large even when the projected feasible set is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the original infimum is finite, uniform objective error at most epsilon limits the optimal-value error to epsilon, sharply; exact feasible-set projection alone gives no objective-gap control.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimal-value distortion satisfies \(|v_g-v_f|\le\varepsilon\), and this bound is sharp; without uniform control no finite universal bound follows.

children.title: Original-Solution Recovery
children.top_down_role: Extraction of visible optimizers from lifted solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Original-Solution Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery by projection when the lifted objective depends only on original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^p\) and let \(C=\pi_x(E)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists y\in\mathbb{R}^p,\ (x,y)\in E\}\). Equip the original problem with \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) and the lifted problem with \(F:E\to\mathbb{R}\), where \(F(x,y)=f(x)\). If \((x^\star,y^\star)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in E}F(x,y)\), then \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\), and the two optimal values are equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting any lifted optimum onto the original variables yields an original optimum, with the same optimal value, when feasibility projects exactly and the objective is unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The lifted problem attains its minimum at \((x^\star,y^\star)\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\) and \(F(x^\star,y^\star)=f(x^\star)=\min_{x\in C}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the lifted formulation.

children.title: Lifted-Witness Recovery
children.top_down_role: Construction or identification of auxiliary witnesses for original solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Witness Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and optimality of witnesses over an original optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^p\), let \(C=\pi_x(E)\), and define \(W(x)=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^p:(x,y)\in E\}\). If \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\), then \(W(x^\star)\neq\varnothing\). Moreover, if \(F:E\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfies \(F(x,y)=f(x)\), then every \(y^\star\in W(x^\star)\) satisfies \((x^\star,y^\star)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in E}F(x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every original optimum has at least one feasible lifted witness, and every such witness forms a lifted optimum when the lifted objective ignores the witness variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W(x^\star)\neq\varnothing\) and \(\{x^\star\}\times W(x^\star)\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in E}F(x,y)\).

notation.meaning: Witness fiber over an original point.
Lifted objective inherited from the original problem.

children.title: Recovery Multiplicity
children.top_down_role: Nonuniqueness of lifted witnesses or visible representatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Recovery Multiplicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicity is measured fiberwise and is independent of objective values within each fiber.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^p\), let \(C=\pi_x(E)\), define \(W(x)=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^p:(x,y)\in E\}\), and let \(X^\star=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\). If \(F:E\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfies \(F(x,y)=f(x)\), then \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in E}F(x,y)=\bigcup_{x\in X^\star}(\{x\}\times W(x))\). Consequently, each \(x\in X^\star\) has exactly \(|W(x)|\) lifted optimal witnesses, and its lifted witness is unique if and only if \(|W(x)|=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lifted optima decompose into witness fibers over original optima; for each original optimizer, the lifted witness is unique exactly when its fiber has one element.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in E}F(x,y)=\bigcup_{x\in X^\star}(\{x\}\times W(x))\), and for every \(x\in X^\star\), witness recovery is unique if and only if \(|W(x)|=1\).

notation.meaning: Fiber of lifted witnesses over an original point.

children.title: Recovery Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cases where feasible or optimal objects lack the required recoverable counterpart.

assumptions_latex: Original recovery is attempted by projecting lifted minimizers onto their \(x\)-coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact recovery is not guaranteed after removing either \(\pi_x(E)=C\) or \(F(x,y)=f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp elementary failures of projection equality or objective preservation.

source_refs.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Both projection equality and objective preservation are essential. If \(C=\{0,1\}\), \(f(x)=-x\), and \(E=\{(0,0)\}\), then the unique lifted point projects to \(0\), although the original minimizer is \(1\); here \(\pi_x(E)\neq C\). Even with \(C=\pi_x(E)=[0,1]\), taking \(E=C\times\{0\}\), \(f(x)=x\), and \(F(x,0)=-x\) makes the lifted minimizer project to \(1\), while the original minimizer is \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery can fail if the lift omits original feasible points or if its objective does not preserve the original objective ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Images of Conic Slices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conic representations as linear images of affine slices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be a convex cone, let \(A:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^q\) be linear, let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^q\), and define \(S=K\cap\{z\in\mathbb{R}^m:Az=b\}\). For a linear map \(P:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^n\), the image has the conic representation \[C=P(S)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists z\in K,\ Az=b,\ x=Pz\}.\] The set \(C\) is convex. Even when \(K\) and \(S\) are closed, \(C\) need not be closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear image of an affine cone slice is convex and has an existential conic representation, but the image need not be closed even when the cone and slice are closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=P(S)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists z\in K,\ Az=b,\ x=Pz\}\) is convex, but closedness of \(K\) and \(S\) does not by itself imply closedness of \(C\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine inverse images of finite-dimensional convex cones.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) and an affine map \(T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) of the form \(T(x)=Ax+b\), the affine preimage construction is \[T^{-1}(K)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax+b\in K\}.\] This set is convex because affine preimages preserve convexity. If \(K\) is closed, then \(T^{-1}(K)\) is closed because \(T\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The points mapped into a convex cone by an affine map form a convex set, which is closed whenever the cone is closed.

children.title: Cone Membership Constraints
children.top_down_role: Conic membership as the lifted feasibility interface.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone Membership Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal membership form and its dual-inequality characterization for closed convex cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be affine with \(T(x)=Ax+b\), and let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be a convex cone. The induced cone-membership constraint is \(Ax+b\in K\), and its feasible set is \(T^{-1}(K)\). If \(K\) is closed and \(K^*=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^m:\langle u,z\rangle\geq0\text{ for every }z\in K\}\), then \[Ax+b\in K\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\langle u,Ax+b\rangle\geq0\text{ for every }u\in K^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone constraint requires an affine image to lie in the cone; for a closed convex cone, this is equivalent to satisfaction of every inequality generated by its dual cone.
assumptions_latex: For the dual characterization, \(K\) is closed and \(K^*=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^m:\langle u,z\rangle\geq0\text{ for every }z\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in T^{-1}(K)\iff Ax+b\in K\); when \(K\) is closed, this is also equivalent to \(\langle u,Ax+b\rangle\geq0\) for every \(u\in K^*\).

notation.meaning: Cone in which the affine image must lie.

children.title: Affine Map Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Interactions between affine map ranges and cone geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in the codomain of \(S\).

notation.meaning: Composition of the two affine maps.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility of affine cone preimages with composition and coordinate changes.

source_refs.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) and \(S:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be affine, with \(T(x)=Ax+b\) and \(S(z)=Bz+c\). For every convex cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\), affine preimages satisfy \[(S\circ T)^{-1}(K)=T^{-1}(S^{-1}(K)).\] Equivalently, \(S(T(x))=(BA)x+(Bb+c)\), so substitution or an affine coordinate change preserves the cone-membership construction whenever domains and codomains match.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine cone preimages commute with composition: imposing membership after two affine maps equals successively taking their preimages.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Map Compatibility

children.title: Empty-Preimage Boundary
children.top_down_role: Range configurations producing infeasible or degenerate preimages.

knowledge_statements.title: Empty-Preimage Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact geometric boundary between feasible and empty affine cone preimages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be linear, let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), define \(T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) by \(T(x)=Ax+b\), and let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be a convex cone. Then \[T^{-1}(K)=\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(b+\operatorname{range}A)\cap K=\varnothing.\] In particular, if \(A=0\), then \(T^{-1}(K)=\mathbb{R}^n\) when \(b\in K\), whereas \(T^{-1}(K)=\varnothing\) when \(b\notin K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine cone preimage is empty precisely when the affine range misses the cone; for a constant map, the preimage is either the whole domain or empty according as its value lies in the cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T^{-1}(K)=\varnothing\iff(b+\operatorname{range}A)\cap K=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Affine map whose cone preimage is considered.
Affine image of the entire domain.

children.title: Homogeneous Product-Cone Lifts
children.top_down_role: Lift architectures built from repeated factors of one cone family.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous Product-Cone Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product lifts whose blocks all use the same cone family and dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,p,q,r\) be positive integers, let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\) be a convex cone, and for \(i=1,\ldots,r\) let \(L_i:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^q\) be affine with \(L_i(x,y)=A_i x+B_i y+c_i\). A homogeneous product-cone lift has the representation \[C=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists y\in\mathbb{R}^p,\ (L_1(x,y),\ldots,L_r(x,y))\in K^r\}.\] Since \(K^r=K\times\cdots\times K\), this is equivalent to requiring \(L_i(x,y)\in K\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,r\). The product \(K^r\) is a convex cone, so the same system is a single-cone lift over \(K^r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated affine constraints over one cone combine into a single constraint over its Cartesian power without changing the represented set.
assumptions_latex: \(n,p,q,r\) are positive integers and \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\) is a convex cone.
For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\), \(A_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\) and \(B_i:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^q\) are linear, \(c_i\in\mathbb{R}^q\), and \(L_i(x,y)=A_i x+B_i y+c_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((L_1(x,y),\ldots,L_r(x,y))\in K^r\iff L_i(x,y)\in K\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\), and the block system is a single-cone lift over \(K^r\).

notation.meaning: Cartesian product of r identical cone factors.

children.title: Mixed-Cone Lifts
children.top_down_role: Lift architectures combining factors from distinct cone families.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Cone Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional lifts using a product of possibly different closed convex cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p,n,q\in\mathbb N_{>0}\), let \(m_i\in\mathbb N_{>0}\) and let \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_i}\) be a closed convex cone for each \(i=1,\ldots,p\). For \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), a mixed-cone lift consists of linear maps \(A_i:\mathbb R^{m_i}\to\mathbb R^q\), a linear map \(B:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^q\) such that
\[
C=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists (y_1,\ldots,y_p)\in\prod_{i=1}^pK_i,\;Bx+\sum_{i=1}^pA_i y_i=b\right\}.
\]
The factors may belong to different cone families; equivalently, this is a lift over the product cone \(K_1\times\cdots\times K_p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-cone lift represents a set by projecting an affine slice of a finite product whose factors may be different cone types.
assumptions_latex: \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_i}\) is a closed convex cone for every \(i=1,\ldots,p\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is the projection of an affine slice of \(\prod_{i=1}^pK_i\).

notation.meaning: The cone used by block i.

children.title: Factorwise Coupling
children.top_down_role: Affine constraints linking separate cone factors.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorwise Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion distinguishing coupled product-cone slices from independent blockwise slices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(K=\prod_{i=1}^pK_i\), an affine slice written as
\[
Bx+\sum_{i=1}^pA_i y_i=b,\qquad y_i\in K_i,
\]
is factorwise uncoupled precisely when, after an invertible change of equation coordinates, its equations partition into systems \(B_i x+A_i' y_i=b_i\), each involving only one cone variable \(y_i\). Otherwise the slice is factorwise coupled. Shared variables \(x\) alone do not establish separability: uncoupling requires a block partition of the affine equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone factors are coupled when no invertible reformulation partitions the affine equations into independent systems, one for each auxiliary cone block.
assumptions_latex: All maps and equation-coordinate changes are finite-dimensional and linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Factorwise coupling holds exactly when the affine equation space admits no stated block partition.

notation.meaning: The auxiliary variable associated with the ith factor.

Moreover, systems sharing x are not independent in the ordinary sense used by the plain statement. A directly supporting source and a precise treatment of equations containing no cone block are required.

children.title: Product Decomposition Boundary
children.top_down_role: Representations whose coupling prevents useful factor separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Product Decomposition Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A product cone does not imply that the represented set decomposes as a Cartesian product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K_1=K_2=\mathbb R_+\) and impose \(y_1=x_1\), \(y_2=x_2\), and \(y_1-y_2=0\). Projection of this affine slice of \(K_1\times K_2\) gives
\[
D=\{(t,t):t\geq0\}.
\]
Although the lifting cone is a product, \(D\) is not \(D_1\times D_2\) for nontrivial subsets \(D_i\subseteq\mathbb R\). Thus Cartesian decomposition of the represented set is guaranteed only when the affine slice and projection also separate factorwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupling equations can destroy Cartesian decomposition even when the lifting cone itself is a product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) has a product-cone lift but no nontrivial Cartesian decomposition across its two coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Structured Conic Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified representation of conic lifts partitioned into finitely many auxiliary blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p,n,q\in\mathbb N_{>0}\), let \(m_i\in\mathbb N_{>0}\), and let \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_i}\) be a closed convex cone for each \(i=1,\ldots,p\). Given linear maps \(A_i:\mathbb R^{m_i}\to\mathbb R^q\), a linear map \(B:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^q\), a block-structured conic lift of \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a representation
\[
C=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists y_i\in K_i\ \text{for }i=1,\ldots,p,\;Bx+\sum_{i=1}^pA_i y_i=b\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, with \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_p)\), the lift is an affine slice of \(K_1\times\cdots\times K_p\) followed by projection onto \(x\). Sparsity or separability is additional structure, not part of the representation itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-structured conic lift partitions finitely many auxiliary variables among cone factors while allowing the affine equations to couple those blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_i}\) is a closed convex cone for every \(i=1,\ldots,p\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is a linear projection of an affine slice of \(K_1\times\cdots\times K_p\).

children.title: Conic Hull Construction
children.top_down_role: Cone generation from scaled copies of a base set.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Hull Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed homogenization of a nonempty closed convex set and its zero-scale recession slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), define its closed homogenization cone by
\[
H_C=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}\{(x,1):x\in C\}.
\]
Then
\[
H_C=\{(t x,t):t>0,\ x\in C\}\cup\{(d,0):d\in\operatorname{rec}(C)\}.
\]
Thus positive-scale points are homogenized copies of points of \(C\), while the zero-scale slice records recession directions. The closure is essential when \(C\) is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed conic hull of the unit-height embedding of a closed convex set contains its scaled points and zero-height recession directions.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_C=\{(t x,t):t>0,\ x\in C\}\cup(\operatorname{rec}(C)\times\{0\})\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conic-Quadratic Homogenization of a Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenization of a nonempty conic-quadratic-representable set, including the closure gap and two exactness regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x\mid \exists u:\ Ax+Bu+b\geq_{\mathbf K}0\}\neq\varnothing\), where \(\mathbf K\) is a direct product of second-order cones. Define \(X^+=\operatorname{cone}\{(x,1)\mid x\in X\}\), \(\widehat X^+=\overline{X^+}\), and \(\widetilde X^+=\{(x,t)\mid t\geq0,\ \exists u:\ Ax+Bu+tb\geq_{\mathbf K}0\}\). Then \(X^+\subseteq\widetilde X^+\subseteq\widehat X^+\). If \(X\) is closed and bounded, then \(\widetilde X^+=X^+=\widehat X^+\), so \(X^+\) is conic-quadratic representable. If \(Bu\in\mathbf K\Rightarrow Bu=0\), then \(\widetilde X^+=\widehat X^+\), so the closed conic hull is conic-quadratic representable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenizing a lifted second-order-cone representation gives a representable set between the embedded conic hull and its closure. It is exact for a closed bounded base set, and it represents the closed conic hull under the stated condition on lifted recession directions.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf K\text{ is a direct product of second-order cones}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X^+\subseteq\widetilde X^+\subseteq\widehat X^+;\quad X\text{ closed and bounded}\Rightarrow\widetilde X^+=X^+=\widehat X^+;\quad (Bu\in\mathbf K\Rightarrow Bu=0)\Rightarrow\widetilde X^+=\widehat X^+.

children.title: Perspective Construction
children.top_down_role: Scale-aware representations of functions or sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Perspective Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed perspective of a proper closed convex function, including its recession value at zero scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex. Its closed perspective is
\[
f^{\pi}(x,t)=
\begin{cases}
t f(x/t),&t>0,\\
f^{\infty}(x),&t=0,\\
+\infty,&t<0,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(f^{\infty}\) is the recession function. Its epigraph satisfies
\[
\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}\{(u,r,1):(u,r)\in\operatorname{epi}f\}.
\]
Hence the closed perspective is the functional form of conic homogenization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective scales a convex function at positive height and uses its recession function at zero height.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}\{(u,r,1):(u,r)\in\operatorname{epi}f\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied. In addition, the conventional coordinate order of epi f^pi is (x,t,r), whereas the conic-hull generators are written (u,r,1); an explicit coordinate permutation or consistently ordered formula is required.

children.title: Base-Slice Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of a nonconic object from a normalized cone slice.

knowledge_statements.title: Base-Slice Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of the original convex set from the unit-height slice of its homogenization cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(H_C=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}\{(x,1):x\in C\}\). Then
\[
H_C\cap\{(z,t):t=1\}=C\times\{1\}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
C=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:(z,1)\in H_C\}.
\]
Thus dehomogenization at unit scale exactly recovers the original set, even when \(C\) is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting a set's closed homogenization cone with the unit-height hyperplane recovers the original set exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex

children.title: Vanishing-Scale Boundary
children.top_down_role: Closure or recession behavior arising at zero scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing-Scale Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification of the zero-height boundary of a closed homogenization cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) with homogenization cone \(H_C=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}(C\times\{1\})\), the vanishing-scale slice is
\[
H_C\cap\{(z,t):t=0\}=\operatorname{rec}(C)\times\{0\}.
\]
Accordingly, a sequence \((t_kx_k,t_k)\in H_C\) with \(t_k\downarrow0\) can have a finite nonzero limit only along recession behavior of \(C\); zero-scale points do not encode ordinary finite points of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zero-height slice of a closed homogenization cone is exactly the recession cone of the original set.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_C\cap\{t=0\}=\operatorname{rec}(C)\times\{0\}\).

children.title: Cone Base Selection
children.top_down_role: Normalized cross-sections used to represent rays of a cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone Base Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact normalized bases of finite-dimensional closed pointed convex cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a nonzero closed pointed convex cone. Choose \(\ell\in\operatorname{int}(K^*)\), so \(\langle\ell,z\rangle>0\) for every \(z\in K\setminus\{0\}\). The normalized cone base selected by \(\ell\) is
\[
B_{\ell}=\{z\in K:\langle\ell,z\rangle=1\}.
\]
It is nonempty, compact, and convex, and every nonzero \(z\in K\) has the unique decomposition \(z=\lambda b\), where \(\lambda=\langle\ell,z\rangle>0\) and \(b\in B_{\ell}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly positive dual functional selects a compact convex cross-section meeting every nonzero cone ray exactly once.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is nonzero, closed, convex, and pointed
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{\ell}=K\cap\{z:\langle\ell,z\rangle=1\}\) is a compact base of \(K\).

notation.meaning: Base selected by the normalizing functional.

children.title: Dehomogenization Maps
children.top_down_role: Maps from homogeneous cone coordinates to normalized objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Dehomogenization Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ray normalization from a positive region of a cone onto an affine base slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a convex cone and let \(\ell\in K^*\). On
\[
K_{\ell}^{+}=\{z\in K:\langle\ell,z\rangle>0\},
\]
define the dehomogenization map
\[
\delta_{\ell}(z)=\frac{z}{\langle\ell,z\rangle}.
\]
Then \(\delta_{\ell}(z)\in B_{\ell}=K\cap\{u:\langle\ell,u\rangle=1\}\), and \(\delta_{\ell}(\alpha z)=\delta_{\ell}(z)\) for every \(\alpha>0\). Hence \(\delta_{\ell}\) identifies each ray meeting the positive region with its unique normalized representative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dehomogenization divides a cone point by a positive linear scale, producing the unique unit-normalized point on the same ray.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_{\ell}(z)\in B_{\ell}\) and \(\delta_{\ell}(\alpha z)=\delta_{\ell}(z)\) for \(\alpha>0\).

notation.meaning: Region of K having positive normalization scale.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 The geometry of cone-lp's: main results p. 37

children.title: Normalization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Alternative slicing choices for compact or noncompact cone geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalization Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of normalization by the position of the functional in the dual cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a nonzero closed convex cone and \(\ell\in K^*\). Normalization by \(\langle\ell,z\rangle=1\) is global exactly when \(\langle\ell,z\rangle>0\) for every \(z\in K\setminus\{0\}\); for closed pointed \(K\), this is equivalent to \(\ell\in\operatorname{int}(K^*)\). If \(\ell\in\partial K^*\), normalization is only partial and excludes \(K\cap\ker\ell\). If \(\ell\notin K^*\), it is not a nonnegative cone normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interior dual functionals normalize every nonzero ray; boundary dual functionals miss zero-valued rays; functionals outside the dual are not cone-positive.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a nonzero closed convex cone
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global, partial, and invalid normalization correspond respectively to strict positivity, boundary dual membership, and failure of dual membership.

notation.meaning: Zero-level hyperplane of the normalizing functional.

children.title: Missing-Base Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cone structures lacking a suitable bounded or globally valid base.

knowledge_statements.title: Missing-Base Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of affine base normalization on cone rays annihilated by the selected functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a convex cone and \(\ell\in K^*\). Any nonzero \(d\in K\cap\ker\ell\) generates a ray \(\{\alpha d:\alpha>0\}\) that never meets \(B_{\ell}=K\cap\{z:\langle\ell,z\rangle=1\}\); consequently, \(z\mapsto z/\langle\ell,z\rangle\) is undefined there. For example, with \(K=\mathbb R_+^2\) and \(\ell(z)=z_1\), the entire ray \(\{(0,t):t>0\}\) is missing from the selected base.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A boundary dual functional misses every cone ray on which it vanishes, so dehomogenization cannot cover the whole cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{\alpha d:\alpha>0\}\cap B_{\ell}=\varnothing\), and dehomogenization is undefined on that ray.

notation.meaning: Unit affine slice selected by ell.
A cone direction annihilated by ell.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Compatible Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines exact recovery of projected recession directions by the homogeneous lifted system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Y,E\) be finite-dimensional inner-product spaces, let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone, and define \(C=\{x\in X:\exists y\in Y,\ b-Ax-By\in K\}\). The lift is recession-compatible when \[\operatorname{rec}C=\operatorname{proj}_{X}\{(d,e)\in X\times Y:-Ad-Be\in K\}.\] The inclusion from the right-hand side into \(\operatorname{rec}C\) always holds; recession compatibility is the reverse inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic lift is recession-compatible when the projection of its homogeneous feasible-direction cone equals the recession cone of the represented set.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone, \(A:X\to E\) and \(B:Y\to E\) are linear, and \(b\in E\).
\(C=\{x\in X:\exists y\in Y,\ b-Ax-By\in K\}\) is nonempty and closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lift is recession-compatible if and only if \(\operatorname{rec}C=\{d\in X:\exists e\in Y,\ -Ad-Be\in K\}\).
