children.title: Protocol-to-Factorization Transfer
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between communication protocols and slack factorizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Protocol-to-Factorization Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer from factorizable terminal contributions to a nonnegative matrix factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\), \(J\), and the terminal-transcript set \(\mathcal{T}\) be finite. Suppose a nonnegative-output protocol computes \(M\in\mathbb{R}_+^{I\times J}\) in expectation and that the expected contribution of every \(\tau\in\mathcal{T}\) is \(u_\tau(i)v_\tau(j)\), with \(u_\tau\in\mathbb{R}_+^I\) and \(v_\tau\in\mathbb{R}_+^J\). Define \(U\in\mathbb{R}_+^{I\times\mathcal{T}}\) and \(V\in\mathbb{R}_+^{\mathcal{T}\times J}\) by \(U_{i\tau}=u_\tau(i)\) and \(V_{\tau j}=v_\tau(j)\). Then \[M_{ij}=\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal{T}}u_\tau(i)v_\tau(j),\qquad M=UV,\qquad \operatorname{rank}_+(M)\le |\mathcal{T}|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factorizable nonnegative expected contributions from finitely many terminal transcripts form a nonnegative factorization with one factor index per transcript.
assumptions_latex: The protocol output is nonnegative and has expectation \(M_{ij}\).
Each terminal expected contribution factors as \(u_\tau(i)v_\tau(j)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M=UV\) with \(U,V\ge0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}_+(M)\le |\mathcal{T}|\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative factors associated with transcript τ
nonnegative factor matrices assembled from terminal contributions

children.title: Randomization Advantage Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where randomized communication complexity differs from deterministic complexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomization Advantage Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates bounded-error Boolean protocols from exact expectation protocols used for factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality function \(\mathrm{EQ}_n(x,y)=\mathbf{1}[x=y]\) on \(\{0,1\}^n\), public-coin bounded-error communication is \(O(1)\) for any fixed error below \(1/2\), whereas deterministic communication is \(n+1\) under the convention that the final answer bit is communicated. This exponential reduction in transcript count does not by itself imply a small exact nonnegative factorization of the equality matrix: that matrix is the identity \(I_{2^n}\), and \[\operatorname{rank}_+(I_{2^n})=2^n.\] Factorization transfer therefore requires exact expectation and nonnegative-output conditions, not merely bounded-error correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality has constant public-coin bounded-error cost but full nonnegative rank, showing that bounded-error randomization alone cannot produce exact small nonnegative factorizations.
assumptions_latex: Public randomness is available for the bounded-error protocol.
The error probability is a fixed constant strictly below \(1/2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R^{\mathrm{pub}}_{\varepsilon}(\mathrm{EQ}_n)=O(1)\) while \(\operatorname{rank}_+(I_{2^n})=2^n\).

notation.meaning: public-coin communication complexity with error ε

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality example is mathematically appropriate for this failure-boundary leaf, and the exact-expectation distinction is correctly stated. Separate authoritative locators are required for the public-coin equality bound, the deterministic cost convention, and the nonnegative rank of the identity matrix.

children.title: Algebraic Lower-Bound Methods
children.top_down_role: Extension lower bounds derived from algebraic invariants or polynomial structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Algebraic Lower-Bound Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minor-based algebraic certificate for nonnegative-rank and polyhedral extension-size lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\in\mathbb{R}_+^{I\times J}\) be finite and let \(r\in\mathbb{N}_0\). Then \[\operatorname{rank}(M)\le\operatorname{rank}_+(M).\] In particular, any nonzero \((r+1)\times(r+1)\) minor of \(M\) certifies \[\operatorname{rank}_+(M)>r.\] If \(M\) is a slack matrix for which an applicable factorization theorem identifies polyhedral extension size with \(\operatorname{rank}_+(M)\), the same minor rules out extensions having at most \(r\) facets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero minor of order r+1 certifies nonnegative rank greater than r and conditionally certifies the corresponding polyhedral extension-size lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The extension conclusion requires an applicable slack-matrix factorization theorem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(M)>r\Rightarrow\operatorname{rank}_+(M)>r\).

children.title: Algebraic-Boundary Certificates
children.top_down_role: Boundary-based algebraic evidence for large or impossible lifts.

knowledge_statements.title: Algebraic-Boundary Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional degree obstruction for a specified class and size of conic lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix dimension \(d\), a lift class \(\mathcal{C}\), and size parameter \(r\). Assume it has been established that every full-dimensional closed convex semialgebraic set admitting a \(\mathcal{C}\)-lift of size at most \(r\) has each irreducible hypersurface component of its algebraic boundary of degree at most \(B_{\mathcal{C}}(r,d)\). If a target set \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) has an irreducible algebraic-boundary component \(V(f)\) with \[\deg f>B_{\mathcal{C}}(r,d),\] then \(P\) admits no \(\mathcal{C}\)-lift of size at most \(r\). The polynomial \(f\), together with the established class bound, is a verifiable obstruction certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An algebraic-boundary component whose degree exceeds the proven degree ceiling for a lift class certifies that no lift of the prescribed size exists.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is full-dimensional, closed, convex, and semialgebraic.
The degree ceiling \(B_{\mathcal{C}}(r,d)\) has been proved for the specified lift class.
\(V(f)\) is an irreducible hypersurface component of the algebraic boundary of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\deg f>B_{\mathcal{C}}(r,d)\Rightarrow P\) has no \(\mathcal{C}\)-lift of size at most \(r\).

children.title: Face-Lattice Obstructions

knowledge_statements.title: Face-Lattice Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-theoretic obstruction to membership in a restricted family of polyhedral extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be polytopes and let \(\pi:Q\to P\) be an affine surjection. The map \[\iota:\mathcal{F}(P)\longrightarrow\mathcal{F}(Q),\qquad \iota(F)=Q\cap\pi^{-1}(F),\] is an injective order embedding. Hence, for a restricted family \(\mathscr{Q}\) of polytopes, if no \(Q\in\mathscr{Q}\) admits an order embedding \(\mathcal{F}(P)\hookrightarrow\mathcal{F}(Q)\), then no member of \(\mathscr{Q}\) is a polyhedral extension of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The face lattice of a polytope order-embeds into the face lattice of every polyhedral extension, so failure of such an embedding excludes a restricted extension family.
assumptions_latex: Candidate extensions use affine surjections \(\pi:Q\to P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl(\forall Q\in\mathscr{Q},\ \mathcal{F}(P)\not\hookrightarrow\mathcal{F}(Q)\bigr)\Rightarrow\) no \(Q\in\mathscr{Q}\) extends \(P\).

notation.meaning: restricted family of candidate extension polytopes

children.title: Symmetric Extensions

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral extension carrying a lifted action of a finite symmetry group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act affinely on a polytope \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\). Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^k\) be a polyhedron and let \(\pi:Q\to P\) be an affine surjection. The extension \((Q,\pi)\) is \(G\)-symmetric if there is an action \(g\mapsto\widetilde g\) of \(G\) on \(Q\) by affine automorphisms such that \[\pi(\widetilde g(y))=g(\pi(y))\qquad\text{for every }g\in G\text{ and }y\in Q.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A G-symmetric polyhedral extension lifts the action of G to affine automorphisms of the extension that commute with its projection.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite group acting affinely on \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((Q,\pi)\) is \(G\)-symmetric exactly when such a commuting lifted group action exists.

notation.meaning: lifted affine automorphism associated with g

children.title: Equivariant Extensions

knowledge_statements.title: Equivariant Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic extension with a cone-preserving lifted representation intertwining the original group action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let a group \(G\) act linearly on \(X\), and let \(P\subseteq X\) be \(G\)-invariant. Let \(K\subseteq Y\) be a closed convex cone, let \(a\in Y\), let \(L\subseteq Y\) be a linear subspace, and let \(\pi:Y\to X\) be linear with \[P=\pi\bigl((a+L)\cap K\bigr).\] This conic representation is \(G\)-equivariant if there is a linear representation \(\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}(Y)\) such that, for every \(g\in G\), \(\rho(g)K=K\), \(\rho(g)(a+L)=a+L\), and \[\pi(\rho(g)y)=g(\pi(y))\qquad\text{for every }y\in(a+L)\cap K.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equivariant conic extension carries a cone-preserving linear action that preserves the affine slice and intertwines the lifted and target actions through the projection.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(G\) acts linearly on \(X\), and \(P\subseteq X\) is \(G\)-invariant.
\(K\subseteq Y\) is a closed convex cone.
\(a\in Y\), \(L\subseteq Y\) is a linear subspace, and \(\pi:Y\to X\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi\circ\rho(g)=g\circ\pi\) on \((a+L)\cap K\), while \(K\) and \(a+L\) are invariant under \(\rho(g)\).

children.title: Unrestricted Extension Size
children.top_down_role: Minimum extension size without symmetry constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathfrak{L}\) is a specified class of admissible conic lifts, each equipped with a size map \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{xc}_{\mathfrak{L}}(P)\) is the infimum of the sizes of admissible lifts representing \(P\), with value \(+\infty\) when none exists; it is a minimum when the infimum is attained.

notation.meaning: Class of admissible conic lifts without symmetry restrictions.
Unrestricted extension size of the represented set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines size relative to a fixed lift class and size convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an admissible lift \(E=(K,L,\pi)\in\mathfrak{L}\), where \(K\) is a closed convex cone, \(L\) is an affine subspace, and \(\pi\) is linear, say that \(E\) represents \(P\) when \(P=\pi(K\cap L)\). The unrestricted extension size is
\[
\operatorname{xc}_{\mathfrak{L}}(P):=\inf\{s(E):E\in\mathfrak{L},\ P=\pi(K\cap L)\}.
\]
The convention is \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). If the size map is integer-valued, every finite infimum is attained and hence is a minimum. No equivariance or symmetry condition is imposed on \(K\), \(L\), or \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unrestricted extension size is the infimum of admissible conic-lift sizes representing the set without imposed symmetry; it is infinite if no such lift exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Unrestricted Extension Size

children.title: Symmetry-Penalty Gaps
children.top_down_role: Size gaps attributable to symmetry restrictions.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is invariant under a group \(G\) acting linearly.
The unrestricted and \(G\)-equivariant lift classes use the same size convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The symmetry penalty is the ratio or difference between optimal \(G\)-equivariant and unrestricted extension sizes.

notation.meaning: Minimum size of a lift equivariant under the full group.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses full group equivariance and permits additive or multiplicative gap reporting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\operatorname{xc}(P)\) be the unrestricted extension size and let \(\operatorname{xc}_{G}(P)\) minimize size only over lifts whose lifted action and projection intertwine the action of \(G\) on \(P\). The multiplicative and additive symmetry penalties are
\[
\Gamma_G(P):=\frac{\operatorname{xc}_{G}(P)}{\operatorname{xc}(P)},\qquad
\Delta_G(P):=\operatorname{xc}_{G}(P)-\operatorname{xc}(P),
\]
whenever the quotient is defined in the extended-real sense. Since every \(G\)-equivariant lift is admissible without the restriction, \(\operatorname{xc}(P)\leq\operatorname{xc}_{G}(P)\), hence \(\Gamma_G(P)\geq1\) for finite positive denominators and \(\Delta_G(P)\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetry-penalty gap compares the smallest fully equivariant lift with the smallest unrestricted lift, multiplicatively or additively.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Penalty Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The comparison fits the symmetry-penalty leaf and the additive inequality is standard, but there is no cited source. The phrase 'whenever the quotient is defined in the extended-real sense' also leaves zero and infinite cases unspecified, so the ratio convention cannot be validated reliably.

children.title: Partial-Symmetry Regimes
children.top_down_role: Intermediate extension families preserving only selected subgroup actions.

assumptions_latex: \(H\leq G\) ranges over subgroups under which lift equivariance may be required.
All equivariant lift classes use the same admissibility and size conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(H_1\leq H_2\leq G\), then \(\operatorname{xc}_{H_1}(P)\leq\operatorname{xc}_{H_2}(P)\).

notation.meaning: Subgroup of symmetries imposed on a lift.
Infimum size among lifts equivariant under the subgroup.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpolates between unrestricted lifts and lifts equivariant under the full group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each subgroup \(H\leq G\), let \(\operatorname{xc}_{H}(P)\) be the infimum of lift sizes subject to \(H\)-equivariance. If \(H_1\leq H_2\leq G\), then
\[
\operatorname{xc}(P)\leq\operatorname{xc}_{H_1}(P)\leq\operatorname{xc}_{H_2}(P)\leq\operatorname{xc}_{G}(P).
\]
Thus subgroup chains define monotone partial-symmetry regimes. Successive differences, and ratios when their denominators are finite and positive, quantify the additional size associated with stronger equivariance requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Requiring equivariance under larger subgroups cannot reduce the optimal lift size, producing monotone regimes between unrestricted and fully symmetric formulations.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Symmetry Regimes

children.title: Exact Extension Size
children.top_down_role: Size requirements for exact lifted representations.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathfrak{L}\) is a fixed class of admissible conic lifts with size map \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{xc}^{\mathrm{exact}}_{\mathfrak{L}}(P)\) is the infimum of the sizes of lifts whose projections equal \(P\) exactly, with value \(+\infty\) if no such lift exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness means set equality, not equality only after closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a lift \(E=(K,L,\pi)\in\mathfrak{L}\), require literal equality \(P=\pi(K\cap L)\). The exact extension size is
\[
\operatorname{xc}^{\mathrm{exact}}_{\mathfrak{L}}(P):=\inf\{s(E):E\in\mathfrak{L},\ \pi(K\cap L)=P\}.
\]
The convention is \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). A lift satisfying only \(P=\operatorname{cl}(\pi(K\cap L))\), or only an inner or outer approximation of \(P\), is not exact unless its projected feasible set already equals \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact extension size is the infimum of lift sizes whose projected feasible sets equal the target itself, without closure or approximation.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Extension Size

children.title: Approximate Extension Size
children.top_down_role: Size requirements for representations permitting controlled approximation.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is a compact convex set with \(0\in\operatorname{int}P\).
\(\varepsilon\geq0\), and approximation is measured by an outer multiplicative sandwich about the origin.
\(\mathfrak{L}\) is a fixed lift class with size map \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{xc}_{\mathfrak{L}}(P;\varepsilon)\) is the least lift size producing \(Q\) with \(P\subseteq Q\subseteq(1+\varepsilon)P\).

notation.meaning: Projected lifted set approximating the target.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses origin-based multiplicative outer approximation for convex bodies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each lift \(E=(K,L,\pi)\in\mathfrak{L}\), write \(Q_E:=\pi(K\cap L)\). The outer \(\varepsilon\)-approximate extension size is
\[
\operatorname{xc}_{\mathfrak{L}}(P;\varepsilon)
:=\inf\{s(E):E\in\mathfrak{L},\ P\subseteq Q_E\subseteq(1+\varepsilon)P\}.
\]
Here \((1+\varepsilon)P:=\{(1+\varepsilon)x:x\in P\}\), and \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). At \(\varepsilon=0\), the sandwich forces \(Q_E=P\), so this convention recovers exact extension size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate extension size minimizes lift size subject to the projected set lying between a convex body and its prescribed multiplicative expansion.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Extension Size

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The origin-based outer multiplicative sandwich is mathematically coherent and the definition fits the leaf, but this is one particular approximation convention rather than a universal one. No source supports the selected convention or notation.

children.title: Exactness-Penalty Gaps
children.top_down_role: Size separations caused by requiring exact representation.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a convex body containing the origin in its interior.
Exact and approximate sizes use the same lift family, size map, and multiplicative outer-approximation convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exactness penalty compares \(\operatorname{xc}(P;0)\) with \(\operatorname{xc}(P;\varepsilon)\), and is nonnegative additively and at least one multiplicatively.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares exact and tolerance-dependent sizes under one approximation convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\varepsilon>0\), define the multiplicative and additive exactness penalties by
\[
\Pi_\varepsilon(P):=\frac{\operatorname{xc}(P;0)}{\operatorname{xc}(P;\varepsilon)},\qquad
D_\varepsilon(P):=\operatorname{xc}(P;0)-\operatorname{xc}(P;\varepsilon),
\]
whenever the quotient is meaningful in the extended-real sense. Every exact representation is an admissible \(\varepsilon\)-approximation, hence \(\operatorname{xc}(P;\varepsilon)\leq\operatorname{xc}(P;0)\). Consequently \(D_\varepsilon(P)\geq0\), and \(\Pi_\varepsilon(P)\geq1\) whenever both sizes are finite and the denominator is positive. A family exhibits an exactness-penalty separation when either gap grows unboundedly with its index.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exactness penalty measures how much larger an exact lift must be than a lift attaining a specified approximation tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Exactness-Penalty Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonic comparison is coherent under the stated approximation convention and the content kind fits the gap leaf. However, the penalty notation and the claim about unbounded family separations have no source, while extended-real quotient cases remain underspecified.

children.title: Approximation-Quality Regimes
children.top_down_role: Extension-size behavior across different approximation quality levels.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a convex body containing \(0\) in its interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The size profile \(f_P\) is nonincreasing in \(\varepsilon\), and tolerance regimes are intervals on which a specified size bound is attainable.

notation.meaning: Smallest tolerance attainable with size at most a budget.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Organizes approximation quality by tolerance and a lift-size budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(0\leq\varepsilon_1\leq\varepsilon_2\), then \((1+\varepsilon_1)P\subseteq(1+\varepsilon_2)P\). Thus every feasible \(\varepsilon_1\)-approximate lift is feasible at \(\varepsilon_2\), and
\[
f_P(\varepsilon_2)\leq f_P(\varepsilon_1).
\]
Equivalently, for a size budget \(m\), define
\[
\varepsilon_P(m):=\inf\{\varepsilon\geq0:f_P(\varepsilon)\leq m\}.
\]
The regime attainable with budget \(m\) is the upper set \(\{\varepsilon:f_P(\varepsilon)\leq m\}\); when its infimum is attained, this set equals \([\varepsilon_P(m),\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowing worse approximation cannot increase minimum lift size; each size budget therefore determines a threshold tolerance and an associated quality regime.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximation-Quality Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonicity and budget-regime formulation are internally correct for the stated origin-based sandwich, and the property kind fits the leaf. No citation supports this selected regime formalization or notation.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{F}\) and \(\mathcal{G}\) are two specified families of closed convex cones with compatible size maps.
\((P_n)\) is a sequence of closed convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A separation occurs when \(\operatorname{xc}_{\mathcal{F}}(P_n)\) and \(\operatorname{xc}_{\mathcal{G}}(P_n)\) have provably different finiteness or asymptotic growth.

notation.meaning: Minimum extension size using cones from the family.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines representability and asymptotic size separations for two cone families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a cone family \(\mathcal{F}\), let \(\operatorname{xc}_{\mathcal{F}}(P)\) be the minimum size of an exact lift of \(P\) using a cone in \(\mathcal{F}\), with value \(+\infty\) if none exists. The sequence \((P_n)\) separates \(\mathcal{F}\) from \(\mathcal{G}\) if either
\[
\operatorname{xc}_{\mathcal{F}}(P_n)<+\infty\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{xc}_{\mathcal{G}}(P_n)=+\infty
\]
for some \(n\), or both quantities are finite and their ratio is unbounded along a subsequence. A directional polynomial-versus-superpolynomial separation is obtained when \(\operatorname{xc}_{\mathcal{F}}(P_n)\leq n^{O(1)}\) but \(\operatorname{xc}_{\mathcal{G}}(P_n)=n^{\omega(1)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone families are separated when one gives finite or asymptotically small lifts for sets that require nonexistent or much larger lifts in the other.
knowledge_statements.title: Separations Between Cone Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is directionally appropriate for the topic, but declaring a sequence-level cone-family separation from a finite-versus-infinite discrepancy at merely 'some' index is not a standard asymptotic criterion without further qualification. The ratio and polynomial-versus-superpolynomial conventions also require a source.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) is \(\mathcal{F}\)-nonrepresentable exactly when no affine slice of any cone in \(\mathcal{F}\) has a linear image equal to \(P\).

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact nonrepresentability relative to a fixed family of finite-dimensional cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The set \(P\) is representable by the cone family \(\mathcal{F}\) if there exist a finite-dimensional cone \(K\in\mathcal{F}\), an affine subspace \(L\) of the ambient space of \(K\), and a linear map \(\pi\) such that
\[
P=\pi(K\cap L).
\]
It is cone-family nonrepresentable when the quantified predicate fails:
\[
\forall K\in\mathcal{F}\;\forall L\;\forall\pi,
\qquad P\neq\pi(K\cap L).
\]
This condition concerns exact equality; it does not exclude representations of \(\operatorname{cl}P\), approximations to \(P\), or lifts using cones outside \(\mathcal{F}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set is nonrepresentable by a cone family when no finite-dimensional affine slice and linear projection of any cone in that family equals it.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Family Nonrepresentability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The prose gives the intended exact nonrepresentability condition and the selected kind fits the failure-taxonomy topic. The displayed universal quantifiers do not explicitly restrict \(L\) to affine subspaces of the ambient space of each \(K\) or \(\pi\) to compatible linear maps, and no source is supplied.

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a fixed closed convex cone.
\(K^m\) denotes the finite Cartesian product of \(m\) copies of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite \(K\)-lift nonexistence means \(P\neq\pi(K^m\cap L)\) for every finite \(m\), affine \(L\), and linear \(\pi\).

notation.meaning: Finite product of the basic cone.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rules out every finite product lift over one basic cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A finite \(K\)-lift of \(P\) consists of an integer \(m\geq1\), an affine subspace \(L\) in the ambient space of \(K^m\), and a linear map \(\pi\) satisfying \(P=\pi(K^m\cap L)\). Finite-lift nonexistence is the condition
\[
\forall m\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq1}\;\forall L\;\forall\pi,
\qquad P\neq\pi(K^m\cap L).
\]
Equivalently, the exact extension size of \(P\) over the product family \(\{K^m:m\geq1\}\) is \(+\infty\). The condition excludes every finite size but makes no assertion about infinite-dimensional representations or approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-lift nonexistence means that no finite product of the chosen cone can represent the target through an affine slice and projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Lift Nonexistence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is internally coherent for the explicitly chosen product family \(\{K^m:m\geq1\}\) and correctly excludes infinite-dimensional and approximate claims. Nevertheless, the identification of 'finite \(K\)-lift' with finite Cartesian powers is convention-dependent and has no cited source; the displayed domains of \(L\) and \(\pi\) are also only supplied in prose.

assumptions_latex: Exact and approximate lifts use one fixed cone family and the sandwich \(P\subseteq Q\subseteq(1+\varepsilon)P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Approximate representability need not imply exact representability; the boundary is witnessed by finite \(\operatorname{xc}(P;\varepsilon)\) for all \(\varepsilon>0\) but \(\operatorname{xc}(P;0)=+\infty\).

notation.meaning: Approximate extension size at positive tolerance.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes positive-tolerance representability from exact finite representability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Exact representability implies \(\varepsilon\)-approximate representability for every \(\varepsilon>0\), because an exact projected set satisfies \(P\subseteq P\subseteq(1+\varepsilon)P\). The converse is not part of the definition and may fail. The expressiveness boundary is characterized by
\[
\operatorname{xc}(P;0)=+\infty,
\qquad
\operatorname{xc}(P;\varepsilon)<+\infty
\quad\text{for every }\varepsilon>0.
\]
More quantitatively, a family \((P_n)\) may have small \(\operatorname{xc}(P_n;\varepsilon)\) for fixed positive \(\varepsilon\) while its exact sizes are infinite or asymptotically much larger. Limits of approximate lifts therefore do not automatically furnish a finite exact lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set may admit finite lifts at every positive tolerance while admitting no finite exact lift; approximation alone does not cross that boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Representation versus Approximation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated finiteness pattern is a suitable failure boundary and the content kind fits the exact-versus-approximation topic. However, the assertion that this pattern may occur is a substantive existence claim, not merely a definition, and no example or authoritative source is cited.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb{S}^2_+\) is the cone of real positive-semidefinite symmetric \(2\times2\) matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linear image \(T(\mathbb{S}^2_+)\) is convex but not closed.

notation.meaning: Linear coordinate projection retaining the first diagonal and off-diagonal entries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete two-dimensional linear image of a closed semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbb{S}^2_+\) be the closed convex cone of real positive-semidefinite symmetric \(2\times2\) matrices, and define
\[
T\!\left(\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{pmatrix}\right):=(a,b).
\]
Then
\[
T(\mathbb{S}^2_+)=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb{R}^2:a>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}.
\]
This convex set is not closed; for example, \((1/n,1)\) belongs to it for every \(n\geq1\), while its limit \((0,1)\) does not. Hence a linear image of a closed convex cone need not be closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting the closed two-by-two positive-semidefinite cone onto its first diagonal and off-diagonal entries gives a convex set that is not closed.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Projection Pathologies

children.title: Improper-Slice Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Geometric failures associated with improperly positioned affine slices.

knowledge_statements.title: Improper-Slice Pathologies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonempty affine slices that miss the relative interior of the lifting cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq E\) be a nonempty closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, and let \(L\subseteq E\) be affine. The slice is improper precisely when \(L\cap K\neq\varnothing\) but \(L\cap\operatorname{ri}K=\varnothing\). Equivalently, the minimal face \(F_{\min}\) of \(K\) containing \(L\cap K\) is a proper face of \(K\). Thus any formulation treating \(K\) itself as the active cone conceals a facial restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible slice is improper when it touches the cone only on its relative boundary, so its feasible points lie in a proper face.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[L\cap\operatorname{ri}K=\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F_{\min}\subsetneq K.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone, let \(L\subseteq E\) be affine, and set \(S=K\cap L\). Define \(F_{\min}\) as the intersection of all faces of \(K\) containing \(S\). A hidden-face pathology occurs when \(S\neq\varnothing\), \(F_{\min}\subsetneq K\), and the representation is nevertheless analyzed over the ambient cone \(K\). Then strict feasibility relative to \(K\) is impossible, whereas \(S\cap\operatorname{ri}F_{\min}\neq\varnothing\). Replacing \(K\) by \(F_{\min}\) identifies the intrinsic active cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hidden face occurs when all lifted feasible points occupy a proper face that the formulation does not explicitly identify.

children.title: Facial-Reduction Diagnostics

knowledge_statements.title: Facial-Reduction Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step exposing certificates for detecting and reducing an improper conic slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(S=\{z\in K:Az=b\}\), where \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone. If there exists \(y\) such that \(w=A^{*}y\in K^{*}\setminus\{0\}\), \(\langle b,y\rangle=0\), and \(K\nsubseteq w^{\perp}\), then every \(z\in S\) satisfies \(\langle w,z\rangle=0\). Hence \(S\subseteq K\cap w^{\perp}\), and \(K\cap w^{\perp}\) is a proper exposed face. Iterating this test until relative strict feasibility holds is facial reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual exposing vector orthogonal to every feasible point certifies that the feasible slice lies in a smaller face.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[S\subseteq K\cap(A^{*}y)^{\perp}\subsetneq K.\]

knowledge_statements.title: Slice–Face Interaction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of affine-conic slices by feasibility and their minimal active face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone and \(L\subseteq E\) affine. Exactly one regime holds: \(L\cap K=\varnothing\); \(L\cap\operatorname{ri}K\neq\varnothing\); or \(L\cap K\neq\varnothing\) while \(L\cap\operatorname{ri}K=\varnothing\). In the second regime the minimal face containing the slice is \(K\). In the third it is a proper face \(F_{\min}\subsetneq K\), and the slice meets \(\operatorname{ri}F_{\min}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine slice is infeasible, relatively strictly feasible in the whole cone, or feasible only within a proper minimal face.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in finite dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[L\cap K=\varnothing\quad\text{or}\quad F_{\min}=K\quad\text{or}\quad F_{\min}\subsetneq K.\]

notation.meaning: minimal face containing the nonempty slice

children.title: Recession-Cone Discrepancies
children.top_down_role: Covers mismatches between recession behavior in the represented set and its lift.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Cone Discrepancies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear images need not commute with recession-cone formation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb R^{2}:t\ge e^{x}\}\) and let \(\pi(x,t)=x\). Then \(C\) is closed and convex, \(\pi(C)=\mathbb R\), and \(\operatorname{rec}(\pi(C))=\mathbb R\). Directly, \(\operatorname{rec}(C)=\{(d_x,d_t):d_x\le0,\ d_t\ge0\}\), so \(\pi(\operatorname{rec}C)=(-\infty,0]\). Consequently the universal inclusion \(\pi(\operatorname{rec}C)\subseteq\operatorname{rec}(\pi C)\) can be strict, even for a closed convex lifted set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting a closed convex set can create recession directions absent from the projection of its lifted recession cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\pi(\operatorname{rec}C)=(-\infty,0]\subsetneq\mathbb R=\operatorname{rec}(\pi C).\]

children.title: Lineality-Space Discrepancies
children.top_down_role: Covers lost, introduced, or distorted lineality directions across representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Lineality-Space Discrepancies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection may create lineality absent from the lifted feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb R^{2}:t\ge e^{x}\}\) and \(\pi(x,t)=x\), the recession cone is \(\operatorname{rec}(C)=\{(d_x,d_t):d_x\le0,\ d_t\ge0\}\). Hence \(\operatorname{lin}(C)=\operatorname{rec}(C)\cap-\operatorname{rec}(C)=\{0\}\). Nevertheless \(\pi(C)=\mathbb R\), so \(\operatorname{lin}(\pi C)=\mathbb R\). Thus \(\pi(\operatorname{lin}C)\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(\pi C)\) may be strict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projection can turn a pointed lifted set into a set containing full lines, so projected and visible lineality spaces differ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\pi(\operatorname{lin}C)=\{0\}\subsetneq\mathbb R=\operatorname{lin}(\pi C).\]

children.title: Recession–Lineality Compatibility Failures
children.top_down_role: Covers failures in the expected structural relation between recession directions and lineality.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession–Lineality Compatibility Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of projection to commute with the intersection defining lineality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every nonempty convex set \(C\) and linear map \(\pi\), \(\operatorname{lin}(C)=\operatorname{rec}(C)\cap-\operatorname{rec}(C)\), and therefore \(\pi(\operatorname{lin}C)\subseteq\pi(\operatorname{rec}C)\cap-\pi(\operatorname{rec}C)\). Compatibility fails whenever this inclusion is strict or \(\pi(\operatorname{rec}C)\subsetneq\operatorname{rec}(\pi C)\). In either case, lineality inferred solely after projection need not correspond to any two-sided lifted recession direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection may fail to preserve both recession directions and their intersection, so visible lineality need not lift to genuine lineality.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty convex subset of a finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\pi\bigl(\operatorname{rec}C\cap-\operatorname{rec}C\bigr)\subseteq\pi(\operatorname{rec}C)\cap-\pi(\operatorname{rec}C),\] with possible strict inclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Lift-Size Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic representation failure measured by minimum cone-lift dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a family of convex sets \((C_n)\), let \(r_K(C_n)\) be the least size parameter \(r\) for which \(C_n\) is the linear image of an affine slice of a cone \(K_r\). The family exhibits lift-size explosion relative to \((K_r)\) when \(r_K(C_n)\) grows superpolynomially in the natural input parameter \(n\); it exhibits exponential explosion when constants \(c>0\) and \(n_0\) satisfy \(r_K(C_n)\ge 2^{cn}\) for all \(n\ge n_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift-size explosion means that every lift from the chosen cone family requires superpolynomially, or exponentially, growing cone size.
assumptions_latex: \((C_n)\) is a family of convex sets with size parameter \(n\).
\((K_r)\) is a size-indexed family of lifting cones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[r_K(C_n)\notin n^{O(1)},\quad\text{or exponentially}\quad r_K(C_n)\ge2^{cn}.\]

notation.meaning: minimum size of a K-lift of C_n

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is precise enough to distinguish superpolynomial and exponential lift-size growth, and the definition role is suitable for the topic. No source is supplied for the extension-complexity terminology or size model, so the record cannot pass source review.

children.title: Dense-Matrix Lift Burden
children.top_down_role: Covers storage, factorization, and operator costs caused by dense lifted matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense-Matrix Lift Burden
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage and coordinate burden of an unstructured semidefinite lift variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dense symmetric lift variable \(X\in\mathbb S^{r}\) has \(r(r+1)/2\) independent scalar coordinates and requires \(\Theta(r^{2})\) scalar storage. If the coefficient matrices defining its affine constraints are themselves dense, storing \(m\) such matrices requires \(\Theta(mr^{2})\) scalars. Thus even when the projected variable is low-dimensional, an explicit dense matrix lift imposes quadratic representation size in the semidefinite block order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unstructured semidefinite block of order r introduces quadratically many scalar entries, multiplied by the number of dense constraint matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S^r\) is stored without sparsity or low-rank compression.
There are \(m\) dense symmetric coefficient matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\dim\mathbb S^r=\frac{r(r+1)}2,\qquad \operatorname{storage}=\Theta(mr^2).\]

notation.meaning: space of real symmetric r by r matrices

children.title: Large-Block Lift Burden
children.top_down_role: Covers computational limits arising from oversized conic or matrix blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Large-Block Lift Burden
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense linear-algebra cost associated with a large positive-semidefinite block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a semidefinite lift containing one dense block \(X\in\mathbb S_{++}^{r}\), evaluating the log-determinant barrier and its Newton derivatives requires a dense factorization of an \(r\times r\) matrix. In the classical dense arithmetic model this factorization uses \(\Theta(r^{3})\) arithmetic operations and \(\Theta(r^{2})\) storage per evaluation, before accounting for assembly or solution of the constraint-space Newton system. A single large block therefore creates a cubic local algebra burden.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single dense semidefinite block of order r requires quadratic storage and cubic factorization work in classical interior-point linear algebra.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_{++}^r\) is treated as a dense block.
Classical dense matrix factorization is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{work}=\Theta(r^3),\qquad \operatorname{storage}=\Theta(r^2).\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity increase caused by merging independent semidefinite blocks.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 Special Cases and Structure Exploitation p. 86

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a semidefinite lift naturally uses \(k>1\) dense blocks of orders \(r_1,\ldots,r_k\), where every \(r_i\ge1\). Separate dense storage scales as \(\Theta(\sum_{i=1}^k r_i^2)\), and separate classical factorizations scale as \(\Theta(\sum_{i=1}^k r_i^3)\). Replacing these blocks by one unstructured block of order \(R=\sum_{i=1}^k r_i\) changes the bounds to \(\Theta(R^2)\) storage and \(\Theta(R^3)\) factorization work. Moreover, \(\sum_{i=1}^k r_i^2<R^2\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^k r_i^3<R^3\), quantifying the burden of lost block structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merging multiple positive-order semidefinite blocks replaces sums of squared and cubed block sizes by the strictly larger square and cube of their total size.

knowledge_statements.title: Poorly Scaled Auxiliary Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-invariant diagnostic based on the best diagonal equilibration of auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a lifted affine system have coefficient operator \(\mathcal A:E_x\times\mathbb R^q\to E_c\), with auxiliary coordinate \(z\). Define its best diagonally equilibrated auxiliary condition number by \(\kappa_{\mathrm{aux}}(\mathcal A)=\inf_{D\succ0\text{ diagonal}}\kappa_2\bigl(\mathcal A\operatorname{diag}(I,D)\bigr)\), where \(\kappa_2\) is computed on the orthogonal complement of the kernel. Relative to a prescribed tolerance \(\tau>1\), the auxiliary space is poorly scaled when \(\kappa_{\mathrm{aux}}(\mathcal A)>\tau\); diagonal rescaling alone then cannot equilibrate its active singular directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An auxiliary space is poorly scaled when even its best positive diagonal coordinate rescaling leaves the active affine operator highly conditioned.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is a finite-dimensional linear operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\kappa_{\mathrm{aux}}(\mathcal A)>\tau.\]

notation.meaning: positive diagonal rescaling of auxiliary coordinates
spectral condition number restricted to active singular directions

children.title: Domain Discrepancies
children.top_down_role: Covers represented points that are incorrectly admitted, excluded, or left unsupported by the lift.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain Discrepancies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detects disagreement between the intended domain and the domain induced by a lifted-conic formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be a proper convex function and let \(L\subseteq X\times\mathbb R\times Y\) be a proposed conic lift of its epigraph. Define \(\widehat E=\{(x,t):\exists y\in Y,\ (x,t,y)\in L\}\) and \(\widehat D=\{x:\exists t\in\mathbb R,\ (x,t)\in\widehat E\}\). A domain discrepancy occurs precisely when \(\widehat D\ne\operatorname{dom}f\). Equivalently, some \(x\) either has a lifted feasible witness although \(f(x)=+\infty\), or belongs to \(\operatorname{dom}f\) but has no lifted feasible witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A domain discrepancy occurs when the lift admits an argument outside the intended effective domain or excludes an argument inside it.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(L\) is the feasible set of the proposed lifted-conic formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat D\ne\operatorname{dom}f\).

notation.meaning: projected epigraph induced by the lift
effective domain of the intended function

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: follows directly from equality of an extended-real function's epigraph domain and the projection induced by a proposed lift

children.title: Closure Discrepancies
children.top_down_role: Covers differences between the intended closure behavior and the set induced by representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Discrepancies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates exact representation from equality obtained only after taking closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq X\) be the intended convex set and let \(L\subseteq X\times Y\) be a proposed lifted-conic feasible set. Write \(P=\{x\in X:\exists y\in Y,\ (x,y)\in L\}\). A closure discrepancy occurs when \(P\ne S\) but \(\operatorname{cl}P=\operatorname{cl}S\). Thus closure equality does not establish exact lifted representation: the symmetric difference \(P\mathbin{\triangle}S\) is nonempty and consists of points whose inclusion status is lost upon closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lift and target have the same closure but are unequal, so closure-based comparison conceals missing or extra points.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\ne S\) and \(\operatorname{cl}P=\operatorname{cl}S\).

notation.meaning: projection of the lifted feasible set

children.title: Boundary-Point Inclusion Failures
children.top_down_role: Covers endpoint or limiting-point membership changes caused by lifting or projection.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Point Inclusion Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A minimal closed-cone lift that incorrectly includes an excluded boundary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take the intended set \(S=(0,\infty)\subset\mathbb R\). Consider the proposed conic lift \(L=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x=y,\ y\in\mathbb R_+\}\) with projection \(\pi_x(x,y)=x\). Its image is \(\pi_x(L)=[0,\infty)\), not \(S\). The discrepancy is exactly the boundary point \(0\): it has the lifted witness \((0,0)\), although \(0\notin S\). Hence replacing strict positivity by membership in the closed nonnegative cone changes boundary-point inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed nonnegative-cone lift of the open positive ray adds zero, demonstrating failure to preserve boundary exclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_x(L)\setminus S=\{0\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed one-dimensional cone calculation directly verifies the counterexample
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Projection-Image Discrepancies
children.top_down_role: Covers projected images that omit intended points or introduce unintended points.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Image Discrepancies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes failure of a lift to recover the target set under its declared projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq X\), let \(L\subseteq X\times Y\) be a lifted feasible set, and let \(\pi_X(x,y)=x\). The lift has a projection-image discrepancy when \(\pi_X(L)\ne S\). The discrepancy decomposes as \(E=\pi_X(L)\setminus S\) and \(M=S\setminus\pi_X(L)\). Points in \(E\) are spurious projected solutions possessing lifted witnesses; points in \(M\) are intended solutions having no lifted witness. Exact projection recovery holds if and only if \(E=M=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection failure consists of extra projected points, missing target points, or both; exactness requires both error sets to be empty.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(S\) is the intended feasible set and \(L\) is the declared lift.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_X(L)\ne S\) if and only if \(E\cup M\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: declared projection onto the original space

children.title: Recovery-Map Discrepancies
children.top_down_role: Covers failures to translate lifted solutions into valid objects in the original representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Recovery-Map Discrepancies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes correct projection from correctness of a claimed witness-recovery map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq X\), let \(L\subseteq X\times Y\), and suppose a proposed recovery map \(R:S\to X\times Y\) is intended to construct lifted witnesses. A recovery-map discrepancy occurs if some \(x\in S\) satisfies either \(R(x)\notin L\) or \(\pi_X(R(x))\ne x\). This failure can occur even when \(\pi_X(L)=S\), because projection exactness asserts existence of a witness for each \(x\), whereas correctness of \(R\) requires the particular witness selected by \(R\) to be feasible and project back to \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even an exact projection may have an invalid recovery rule if that rule returns an infeasible witness or the wrong original point.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is defined on every point of \(S\).
\(\pi_X:X\times Y\to X\) is the declared projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x\in S:\ R(x)\notin L\ \text{or}\ \pi_X(R(x))\ne x\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the criterion is the direct negation of feasibility and right-inverse requirements for a recovery map
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Lifted-Witness Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Covers nonunique or incompatible lifted witnesses that obstruct reliable recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Witness Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies nonuniqueness of auxiliary variables over a fixed represented point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\subseteq X\times Y\) represent \(S=\pi_X(L)\). For \(x\in S\), define the witness fiber \(W(x)=\{y\in Y:(x,y)\in L\}\). Lifted-witness ambiguity occurs at \(x\) exactly when \(W(x)\) contains at least two distinct elements. The lift has globally unique witnesses exactly when every fiber is a singleton; equivalently, there exists a unique map \(r:S\to Y\) satisfying \(L=\{(x,r(x)):x\in S\}\). Ambiguity alone does not imply projection failure, since all witnesses in one fiber project to the same \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A represented point is witness-ambiguous when two distinct auxiliary assignments certify it; this need not impair the projected set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is witness-ambiguous if and only if \(|W(x)|>1\).

notation.meaning: fiber of lifted witnesses above the point x
unique auxiliary-variable selection when it exists

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: witness ambiguity is the standard non-singleton-fiber property of a projection
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Projection–Recovery Exactness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Covers regimes where projection remains faithful but recovery guarantees weaken or fail.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection–Recovery Exactness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the exact conditions separating set recovery from constructive witness recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq X\), let \(L\subseteq X\times Y\), and define \(\pi_X(x,y)=x\). A map \(R:S\to X\times Y\) is an exact recovery map when \(R(x)\in L\) and \(\pi_X(R(x))=x\) for every \(x\in S\). Existence of such a map implies \(S\subseteq\pi_X(L)\). Projection exactness, meaning \(\pi_X(L)=S\), holds if and only if \(\pi_X(L)\subseteq S\) and an exact recovery map exists, provided set-theoretic selection from the nonempty witness fibers is permitted. Uniqueness or continuity of the recovery map requires additional hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact recovery supplies a feasible lifted witness for every target point but does not exclude spurious projected points. Exact projection additionally requires that every projected point belongs to the target.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
Set-theoretic selection from nonempty witness fibers is permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_X(L)=S\) if and only if \(\pi_X(L)\subseteq S\) and there exists \(R:S\to X\times Y\) such that \(R(S)\subseteq L\) and \(\pi_X\circ R=\operatorname{id}_S\).

notation.meaning: recovery map selecting a lifted feasible point
identity map on the target set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact recovery is a section of the projection restricted to the lifted feasible set, while image equality additionally excludes spurious projected points

knowledge_statements.title: Representation-Language Incompleteness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes inability of a fixed conic modeling language to express every target in a chosen class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a family of permitted cones \(\mathcal K\) and let \(\operatorname{Rep}(\mathcal K)\) be the sets obtainable as linear images of affine slices of finite products of cones from \(\mathcal K\). For a target class \(\mathcal C\) of convex sets, the representation language generated by \(\mathcal K\) is incomplete for \(\mathcal C\) when \(\mathcal C\nsubseteq\operatorname{Rep}(\mathcal K)\); equivalently, there exists \(S\in\mathcal C\) admitting no finite lifted-conic representation using only the permitted cones, affine constraints, and linear projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic language is incomplete for a target class when at least one target has no finite representation using its permitted constructions.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal K\) is a fixed family of convex cones.
Only finite products, affine slices, and linear images are allowed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists S\in\mathcal C:\ S\notin\operatorname{Rep}(\mathcal K)\).

notation.meaning: sets expressible in the fixed lifted-conic language

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: incompleteness is defined by strict containment of the expressible class within the target class

children.title: Representation Diagnostic Signatures
children.top_down_role: Observable structural signatures used to distinguish representation failures.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Diagnostic Signatures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Packages set, closure, recovery, and fiber tests into a verifiable representation diagnostic signature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a target \(S\subseteq X\), a lift \(L\subseteq X\times Y\), and a proposed recovery map \(R:S\to X\times Y\), define \(W(x)=\{y\in Y:(x,y)\in L\}\) and the diagnostic signature \(\Sigma=(E,M,C,Q,A)\), where \(E=\pi_X(L)\setminus S\), \(M=S\setminus\pi_X(L)\), \(C=\operatorname{cl}(\pi_X(L))\mathbin{\triangle}\operatorname{cl}S\), \(Q=\{x\in S:R(x)\notin L\ \text{or}\ \pi_X(R(x))\ne x\}\), and \(A=\{x\in S:|W(x)|>1\}\). An exhibited member of \(E\), \(M\), \(C\), or \(Q\) certifies the corresponding projection, closure, or recovery failure. A member of \(A\) certifies witness ambiguity. The equality \(A=\varnothing\) means that every fiber has at most one witness; together with \(E=M=\varnothing\), it implies that every target point has exactly one witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The signature records extra, missing, closure-mismatched, recovery-failing, and witness-ambiguous points. Absence of ambiguity gives at most one witness per point, while projection exactness additionally supplies witness existence.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(R\) is defined on every point of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E=M=\varnothing\) is equivalent to projection exactness, \(C=\varnothing\) is equivalent to closure equality, \(Q=\varnothing\) is equivalent to correctness of \(R\), and \(A=\varnothing\) is equivalent to every \(W(x)\) having at most one element.

notation.meaning: extra, missing, closure, recovery, and ambiguity diagnostics

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the signature synthesizes exact set-difference, closure, recovery, and fiber predicates

children.title: Boundary Localization
children.top_down_role: Localization of failure sources within lift geometry, scale, or semantics.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Localization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Determines when all projection errors are confined to the target boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq X\) be convex and let \(P=\pi_X(L)\) be the image of a proposed lift. The projection discrepancy is localized to the boundary of \(S\) exactly when \(P\mathbin{\triangle}S\subseteq\operatorname{bd}S\). Equivalently, \(P\cap\operatorname{int}S=\operatorname{int}S\) and \(P\setminus S\subseteq\operatorname{bd}S\). If additionally \(\operatorname{cl}P=\operatorname{cl}S\), then every remaining exactness failure concerns inclusion or exclusion of boundary points rather than disagreement on interior points or on the common closed hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrepancy is boundary-localized when the lift agrees with the target throughout its interior and differs only on target-boundary points.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\mathbin{\triangle}S\subseteq\operatorname{bd}S\).

notation.meaning: projected image of the proposed lift
topological boundary of the target set
